(2) In src/client/Controllers/NotificationController.luau, show the remaining time in the alert subtitle, read from the TheftEndsAt attribute of the Workspace.Vehicles model whose TheftVictimUserId == LocalPlayer.UserId. Speed debuffs, remote DriveCar and paying a bonus on a victim-caused wreck are balance choices. A wreck bonus should only ship together with F2's per-pair cap, or it becomes another farm.

summary: The '🔨 B knocked A out of B's <car>!' EventFeed line never fires on a normal knock-out, because the eject happens before onThiefHit records the hitter.
evidence: CombatService.applyHit stuns the victim (879), then ejects (880-881), and only then calls TheftService.onThiefHit (885). eject runs setDriver(nil), which fires DriverChanged. Signal:Fire runs handlers immediately through task.spawn (Signal.luau:48-56), so TheftService.onDriverChanged runs markDropped (TheftService.luau:1489-1497) before onThiefHit. In markDropped, `local hitter = theft.lastHitBy` is still nil (initialised at 1151), so the EventFeed block at 900-908 is skipped. The knocked flag only comes out right because the Stunned attribute is set first.
failureScenario: B bonks A out of B's Epic. The server never broadcasts a knock-out line, so one of the 'moments worth clipping' from pillar 3 is silently lost on every first hit.
suggestedFix: In applyHit, call TheftService.onThiefHit(attacker, victim) before VehicleService.eject (move line 885 above 880). Alternatively, have markDropped read the hitter from CombatService's last hit or task.defer the feed line.
verifyReason: Confirmed. In CombatService.applyHit (~877-885) the order is stun, then callSystem('VehicleService','eject',car), then callSystem('TheftService','onThiefHit',...). eject runs setDriver(car,nil) synchronously, which calls DriverChanged:Fire. Signal:Fire uses task.spawn, which runs the handler immediately, so TheftService.onDriverChanged runs markDropped before onThiefHit. markDropped does not yield before `local hitter = theft.lastHitBy`, which is still nil on the first hit (initialised nil in beginTheft and on takeover), so the EventFeed block is skipped. knocked is still correct because CombatService.stun sets the Stunned attribute first. The impact is cosmetic only (a missing feed line), so low.
fix: src/server/Systems/CombatService.luau applyHit: move `callSystem("TheftService", "onThiefHit", attacker, victim)` to just before `if car then callSystem("VehicleService", "eject", car) end`. onThiefHit only sets lastHitAt and lastHitBy and pays revenge, so nothing in it depends on the eject. Add a theft.spec case that a hit followed by a drop fires the EventFeed.

summary: After a drop, the thief's HUD keeps showing 'DELIVER IT HOME! 1:42' while the car will actually be towed in 12-20s.
evidence: TheftService.sendThiefState sends dropped and droppedEndsAt (TheftService.luau:539-548). StateController.sanitizeTheft keeps only active, endsAt, carId and targetPlot (StateController.luau:86-96). HUDController.applyTheft and refreshTheft (HUDController.luau:1303-1341) therefore always count down the 150s endsAt. The HUD integration doc already lists this as a deviation that was never applied.
failureScenario: A is bonked out and sees 1:30 left on the HUD, so does not hurry. 20s later the car disappears. The only hints were a 4-second toast and a waypoint label.
suggestedFix: Keep dropped and droppedEndsAt in sanitizeTheft. In the HUD, switch to a red 'GET BACK IN! 0:12' state using droppedEndsAt while dropped.
verifyReason: Confirmed. sendThiefState sends dropped and droppedEndsAt (TheftService.luau ~539-548), but StateController.sanitizeTheft (~86-96) keeps only active, endsAt, carId and targetPlot, and the TheftState type has no dropped field. HUDController.applyTheft and refreshTheft always count down the 150s endsAt. This is listed as a deviation in gameplay-client.md:334. Downgraded to low because the thief does get a 4s toast with the real tow time and the waypoint label switches to 'GET BACK IN!'.
fix: src/client/Controllers/StateController.luau: add `dropped = raw.dropped == true` and `droppedEndsAt = num-or-nil(raw.droppedEndsAt)` to sanitizeTheft and to the TheftState type. src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau: in applyTheft store the dropped state; in refreshTheft, while dropped, use droppedEndsAt with the label/colour 'GET BACK IN! 0:12' (Danger) instead of endsAt. Extend the clientcore.spec sanitizeTheft case.

summary: A victim can always cancel a theft by leaving (and rejoin to get the car back with offline earnings). The car disappears from under the thief with no compensation, and the thief keeps the wanted star.
evidence: onPlayerRemoving (TheftService.luau:1575-1584) and the tick (1527-1529) call failTheft(theft,'victim_left'). This destroys the car (645-647) and skips the restore (649-651); the thief only gets the toast '😶 X left. The {car} vanished!' (_failText 387-388). DataService.release fires Releasing (DataService.luau:1079) before the final writeAsync (1082), so a transfer could be hooked in at that point.
failureScenario: A has driven B's Mythic most of the way home. B leaves the game, A's car vanishes mid-drive, A keeps +1 star and cops, and gets nothing. B rejoins with the Mythic. This contradicts 'fair theft' and makes stealing from experienced players pointless.
suggestedFix: Hook DataService.Releasing. If the theft has run more than N seconds, or the thief is outside the victim's garage, remove the record from the victim's data before the final save and give it to the thief (storeCar or a pending queue), with the usual uncollected payout. At minimum, pay the thief chopValue and clear their wanted level.
verifyReason: Confirmed. onPlayerRemoving and _tick call failTheft(theft,'victim_left'), which destroys the car and skips restoreVictimSlot. The record never left the victim's data, and the thief only gets '😶 X left. The {car} vanished!' while keeping the theft heat. However, this is spec-sanctioned: SPEC §6 TheftService says fail is 'Triggered by: time limit, victim leaving (car vanishes, thief notified)', which is consistent with pillar 5 ('Offline garages can't be robbed'). The victim also pays a real cost (leaving the server and plot). So this is a design trade-off, not a bug. Moving the car on DataService.Releasing is risky: it adds a data-ordering dependency and gives alts a way to transfer cars instantly without delivering.
fix: If the team wants to change it, first update docs/SPEC.md §6 TheftService. Then the minimal change in src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau failTheft for reason 'victim_left': if online(thief) and the car is outside the victim's plot, or hooks.clock() - theft.startedAt >= ~30s, pay the thief a consolation (e.g. EconomyMath.chopValue(carId, mutation), capped) through DataService.addCash, and call WantedService to remove the playerTheft heat added for this theft. Do not move the car record on Releasing.

summary: The Steal prompt is shown, and the full hold is required, even when the server will refuse: victim on cooldown, victim already being robbed, or the thief's garage is full.
evidence: GarageClient.updatePrompts enables Steal based only on mine, driving, locked and CarCount (GarageClient.luau:135-139). The refusals with codes victimBusy, cooldown and full (TheftService.luau:342-350) only run after the hold, from steal.Triggered then beginTheft (GarageService.luau:555-576). There is no replicated cooldown or busy attribute on the plot, and the thief's own free-slot count from the snapshot is not checked.
failureScenario: Right after C robbed B, A holds E for 3.5s on B's Epic and gets '⏳ They were just robbed — try again in 12s'. With a full garage, A holds 3.5s and gets 'Your garage is full!'. The player could not have known in advance.
suggestedFix: Server: set plot attributes RobbableAt (cooldown end, server time) and BeingRobbed. Client: disable the Steal prompt or set its ObjectText to 'PROTECTED 0:12' / 'BEING ROBBED' / 'YOUR GARAGE IS FULL', using those attributes and the local snapshot's free slots.
verifyReason: Confirmed. GarageClient.updatePrompts enables Steal on `not mine and not driving and not locked and cars >= NEWBIE_PROTECTION_CARS` only. victimBusy, cooldown and full are only checked server-side in _canSteal after the hold completes (steal.Triggered then beginTheft). The cooldown is not replicated anywhere. 'Busy' could be derived from the existing pad State='BeingStolen' attributes, but the client does not do this. The thief's free slots are in the local snapshot but are not checked. The cost is a wasted hold (1.1s up to 8.4s) followed by a clear error toast, so this is UX, low severity.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau: in setCooldown, also set a plot attribute `RobbableAt` = toServerTime(cooldownUntil) on PlotService.getPlotModel(plotIndexOf(victim)). src/client/Controllers/GarageClient.luau updatePrompts: also disable Steal when any pad in view.model has State == 'BeingStolen', when Workspace:GetServerTimeNow() < RobbableAt, or when StateController's snapshot shows no free slots. Re-run updatePlotPrompts on a short timer or attribute change so the prompt re-enables when RobbableAt passes.

summary: The daily contract 'Bonk 3 thieves out of cars' only counts when the attacker is the victim of that exact theft. Players need to be robbed 3 times in one UTC day and catch each thief, so the contract is effectively uncompletable.
evidence: CombatService.luau:869-870 sets `defended = car ~= nil and car.kind == 'Stolen' and stealingFromAttacker`, and progress('defend') only runs when defended is true (886-889). Economy.luau:177 defines { id='bonk3', text='Bonk 3 thieves out of cars', stat='defend', goal=3 }. A bystander (C) bonking a thief (A) does not count.
failureScenario: A player rolls bonk3 and spends the day hunting thieves. Bonking other players' thieves does not count, so the contract never progresses, which hurts the daily-contract retention pillar.
suggestedFix: Count any hit that ejects the driver of a Stolen car (or of a Loot car whose driver has Wanted ≥ 1). Keep the extra 'THIEF BONKED' message for the victim.
verifyReason: Confirmed. CombatService.applyHit sets `defended = car ~= nil and car.kind == 'Stolen' and stealingFromAttacker`, and isStealingFrom requires theft.victim == attacker. 'defend' is the only source of that stat (grep finds just CombatService.luau:887). The code matches SPEC §6 CombatService line 180 ('contract defend if that ejected a thief driving the attacker's stolen car'), so the defect is in the contract design. 'Bonk 3 thieves out of cars' needs the player to be robbed 3 times in one UTC day and to catch each thief while still seated. Players under 3 cars can never be robbed. The contract is therefore dead whenever it is rolled, and there is no reroll.
fix: src/server/Systems/CombatService.luau applyHit: compute `thiefEjected = car ~= nil and (car.kind == 'Stolen' or (car.kind == 'Loot' and (tonumber(victim:GetAttribute('Wanted')) or 0) >= 1))` and call RewardsService.progress(attacker,'defend',1) when thiefEjected. Keep the 'THIEF BONKED! Go grab your car back!' notify only when `defended`. Update docs/SPEC.md line 180 to match. Stun immunity (immuneUntil) already limits repeat-bonk farming of the same target.

summary: beginTheft and takeover treat 'seat() did not throw' as success. VehicleService.seat returns (false, reason) and never throws, so a failed seating starts or 'resumes' a theft with nobody in the car.
evidence: call() returns (pcallOk, firstResult) (TheftService.luau:160-172). beginTheft uses `local seatOk = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief)` (1190), which is true whenever the pcall succeeds. takeover's `local seatOk, err = call(...)` (971-974) only warns when the pcall fails. VehicleService.seat returns false with 'no character', 'occupied' or 'sit failed' (VehicleService.luau:908-918, 949-956) without throwing.
failureScenario: A's character dies or resets the moment the hold completes. The theft starts anyway: the slot shows STOLEN, A gets +1 star, B's alarm fires, and after 2s B gets 'Your car was dropped! Grab it back in 12s!'. On takeover, C sees 'GO GO GO!' and the drop prompts are cleared even if C was not seated, until the next tick drops the car again.
suggestedFix: Use `local okCall, seated = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief)` and, if seated ~= true, run failTheft(theft,'error') (in beginTheft) or keep the car dropped and skip clearDropped (in takeover).
verifyReason: Confirmed. call() returns (pcallOk, result). beginTheft does `local seatOk = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief)`, which captures only pcallOk. takeover only warns when the pcall fails. VehicleService.seat returns (false, 'gone' | 'player' | 'not allowed' | 'no character' | 'occupied' | 'sit failed') and never throws. This is already documented in vehicles-world.md:311. The impact is limited. gatherState checked that the thief is alive moments before, with no realistic yield in between (spawn is synchronous), so a seat failure is rare. If it happens, the _tick safety net marks the car dropped after SEAT_GRACE. The visible symptom is a theft that started with nobody in the car (alarm, heat, 'dropped' toast).
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau beginTheft: `local okCall, seated = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief); if not okCall or seated ~= true then failTheft(theft,'error') ... return false end` (the existing failure branch). In takeover, seat before clearing the drop state: if driverOf(car) ~= player, call seat; if it does not return true, notify the player 'Try again!' and return false without calling clearDropped (the prompts stay up). Otherwise clearDropped and continue.

summary: The free slot is checked only when the theft starts, not reserved. If it is filled during the theft (claiming a Playtime or Daily car from the menu while driving, or an owed Diamond Dragster being auto-delivered), delivery is refused and the thief has no way to sell from the car.
evidence: complete() refuses when freeSlots <= 0 (TheftService.luau:1248-1255) and the delivery is simply retried every 3s. storeCar uses the first free slot (GarageService.luau:745-747), so reward grants take the slot. The SellCar and DriveCar remotes exist (GarageService.luau:1296-1307), but no client code fires them; the only client-fired garage remote is LockGarage (GarageClient.luau:659). Selling therefore needs the on-foot SellPrompt, which means leaving the car, starting the 12s abandon timer and giving the victim a Recover prompt.
failureScenario: A, with 1 free slot, claims the 15-minute Rare gift while driving B's Epic and then reaches the drop-off. A sees 'Garage full! Sell a car to park this one. Hurry!', has to jump out and run to a display car, and B recovers the Epic.
suggestedFix: Reserve the slot at beginTheft (GarageService.reserveSlot or a pending marker that _firstFreeSlot respects), or let complete() overflow into a pending queue the way exclusives already work. Alternatively, have RewardsService and MonetizationService send cars to pending while the player has an active theft.
verifyReason: Confirmed but mostly self-inflicted. complete() refuses when freeSlots <= 0 and only notifies (throttled to 3s). storeCar takes the first free slot. No client fires SellCar or DriveCar (the client remotes are BuyTool, BuyUpgrade, ClaimDaily, ClaimPlaytime, GoHome, LockGarage, Rebirth, RedeemCode, SetSetting, ToolAction, TutorialDone, UnlockSlot), so selling needs the on-foot SellPrompt. The paths that fill a slot mid-theft are a player-initiated ClaimPlaytime or ClaimDaily car, or MonetizationService's periodic deliverExclusives loop. The latter only matters if the thief sold a car and started a theft before the next exclusive check. In the thief's own garage, hopping out to sell gives a 12s window, and the victim would need to be at the thief's garage to Recover, so the claimed loss is unlikely.
fix: Cheapest: in src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau (car grants) and src/server/Systems/MonetizationService.luau deliverExclusives, skip or defer car grants while TheftService.getActiveTheft(player) ~= nil and GarageService.freeSlots(player) <= 1. Rewards should stay claimable later, or fall back to the existing owed/cash fallback. Alternatively, let TheftService.complete treat a full garage like exclusives: remove the record from the victim and queue it as owed for the thief.

summary: The transfer is atomic in memory but saved as two separate, unordered DataStore writes. A hard server crash between them can duplicate the car (thief saved, victim not) or lose it.
evidence: TheftService.luau:1329-1336 starts saveNow(thief) and saveNow(victim) in two independent task.spawn calls. saveNow → writeAsync (DataService.luau:1034-1040) waits out the ~6s per-key cooldown independently for each key. BindToClose covers a graceful shutdown but not a crash.
failureScenario: The victim autosaved 2s ago, so their write waits about 4s, while the thief's write lands at once. The server crashes in that window, and both players load with the same car.
suggestedFix: Save sequentially in one task, victim first (removal), then thief. Better: stamp a transferId in both profiles and reconcile on load (if the victim still holds a record whose transferId the thief has, drop it).
verifyReason: Confirmed in principle. complete() starts saveNow(thief) and saveNow(victim) in two independent hooks.spawnTask calls. Each writeAsync respects its own per-key write rate, so the order is not defined. A hard server crash between the two writes can duplicate the car (thief saved, victim not) or lose it. BindToClose covers a graceful shutdown, and a player cannot trigger a crash on purpose, so this is a rare edge case. Low.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau complete(): replace the two spawns with one `hooks.spawnTask(function() pcall(DS.saveNow, victim); pcall(DS.saveNow, thief) end)`. Saving the removal first means a crash can at worst lose the car rather than duplicate it, which matters more for the economy. A transferId reconcile-on-load is optional hardening in DataService.luau.

summary: Wreck, bust and thief-leave all eject before the theft is failed, so the victim is first told the car was 'dropped, grab it in 20s' and then something different. Recover and Hotwire prompts are also put back onto a wrecked car, and recovering it pays the bonus.
evidence: VehicleService.wreck disables every prompt (VehicleService.luau:1319-1323) and then calls eject (1325). DriverChanged runs markDropped, which adds fresh, enabled drop prompts (TheftService.luau:882) and notifies the victim (887-895). The car is destroyed 2s later (1355-1357). The RecoverPrompt handler (TheftService.luau:761-774) does not check car.wrecked. WantedService.handleCar ejects (WantedService.luau:413) before TheftService.fail (417). VehicleService.onPlayerRemoving clears the driver (VehicleService.luau:1684-1688; connected in init before TheftService's handler at TheftService.luau:1618).
failureScenario: A crashes the Epic hard. B gets 'Your car was dropped! Grab it back in 20s!', runs over within 2s, holds Recover on the burning wreck and gets 'RECOVERED! +bonus' instead of 'wrecked... towed home'. When A is busted, B gets two contradictory toasts at once.
suggestedFix: In onDriverChanged, skip markDropped if car.wrecked or car.destroyed, or if the old driver is no longer online. Check car.wrecked in the RecoverPrompt handler. In WantedService.handleCar, call TheftService.fail before VehicleService.eject.
verifyReason: Confirmed. VehicleService.wreck disables prompts and then calls eject, which runs setDriver(nil) and DriverChanged (synchronous via task.spawn), and onDriverChanged runs markDropped. markDropped creates fresh, enabled Recover and Hotwire prompts and sends the victim 'dropped! Grab it back in 12s'. The car is destroyed WRECK_DESTROY_AFTER=2s later, then onDestroyed calls failTheft('wrecked'). The RecoverPrompt handler does not check car.wrecked, so a victim within reach during those 2s gets the full bonus. The Hotwire prompt shows but is a no-op, because addStealPrompt's Triggered checks car.wrecked. _tick would also call markDropped on a wrecked car. WantedService.handleCar ejects (~413) before TheftService.fail (~417), so the victim gets two contradictory toasts. For thief_left, VehicleService.onPlayerRemoving clears the driver, and during PlayerRemoving the player is still parented to Players, so markDropped treats them as online. Whether the toast appears depends on handler order. All of these are cosmetic or minor.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau: at the top of markDropped add `local c = theft.car; if type(c) == 'table' and (c.wrecked or c.destroyed) then return end` (this covers both the signal and the _tick path). In the RecoverPrompt Triggered handler, return early if car.wrecked or car.destroyed. src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau handleCar: for car.kind == 'Stolen', call TheftService.fail(car,'busted') before VehicleService.eject (fail destroys and ejects anyway). For thief_left, optionally defer markDropped in onDriverChanged (task.defer, then re-check theft.finished) so the PlayerRemoving fail wins.

summary: The victim's live 'YOUR CAR' arrow finds the thief by name, and the payload is a DisplayName. Duplicate DisplayNames, or another player's username matching it, make the arrow point at the wrong player.
evidence: TheftService sends CarStolenAlert(victim, nameOf(thief), ...) where nameOf returns the DisplayName (TheftService.luau:247-252, 1202). findPlayerByName (NotificationController.luau:1201-1213) first compares p.Name == name, then DisplayName. thiefPosition (1216-1242) tracks the matched player's seat or root. The car already carries TheftVictimUserId (TheftService.luau:1180).
failureScenario: There are two players with the DisplayName 'Alex' (common), or the thief's DisplayName equals another player's username. B's arrow leads to the wrong person while the real thief escapes.
suggestedFix: Track the car itself: on the client, find the model in Workspace.Vehicles whose TheftVictimUserId == LocalPlayer.UserId and TheftActive == true, and pass it to WaypointController.track. This also follows dropped cars and hijacks. Alternatively, add thiefUserId and VehicleId to the CarStolenAlert payload.
verifyReason: Confirmed. CarStolenAlert carries nameOf(thief), which is the DisplayName. NotificationController.findPlayerByName first matches p.Name == name and then the first p.DisplayName == name. thiefPosition follows that player's seat or root (and alertLastCar). Duplicate DisplayNames, or a username equal to the thief's DisplayName, point the arrow at the wrong player. This is rare in an 8-player server. The car already carries TheftVictimUserId, TheftThiefUserId and TheftActive attributes.
fix: src/client/Controllers/NotificationController.luau thiefPosition: first look in Workspace.Vehicles for a Model with TheftActive == true and TheftVictimUserId == Players.LocalPlayer.UserId and return its pivot. This also covers dropped and hijacked cars. Keep the name lookup only as a fallback. No server change is needed.

summary: A 15s re-arm against locks of 45-120s (+10s per rebirth) lets an AFK owner with a tap macro keep the garage locked 75-90% of the time. Together with offline protection, wealthy players become nearly unrobbable and the theft content dries up.
evidence: PlotService.LOCK_REARM = 15 (PlotService.luau:38), applied in unlock (1269-1281). tryLock only requires being inside the garage and the lock being ready (1331-1358). Lock values are { 45, 60, 90, 120 } in Economy.Upgrades.lock, plus 10s per rebirth (_lockDuration 245-247). The LockGarage remote allows 2 per second (1568-1570).
failureScenario: A level-3 lock owner AFKs in the garage with an autoclicker on 'LOCK GARAGE'. Thieves get a 15s window every 135s and must also cover the hold time and the walk in.
suggestedFix: Make the re-arm proportional (e.g. equal to the lock duration, for at most 50% uptime). Alternatively, give a fixed number of charges per 10 minutes, or require no lock while the owner has been idle for 2+ minutes.
verifyReason: Confirmed arithmetic. LOCK_REARM = 15 against lock values {45,60,90,120} + 10/rebirth gives 75% to 89%+ uptime for an owner who re-presses at once. The LockGarage remote allows 2/s, and the LockButton pad also locks on Touched, so idle-animation touches from an AFK owner standing on the pad may re-lock without a macro. The re-arm was added on purpose (economy-server.md:117), and a guaranteed 15s window plus the theft hold is a tuning choice. High lock uptime is common in the genre. This is a balance issue, not a defect.
fix: src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau: make the re-arm proportional, e.g. `st.lockReadyAt = os.clock() + math.max(PlotService.LOCK_REARM, 0.5 * lastDuration)` (store the duration in lockFor or tryLock) and mirror it in the LockReadyAt attribute. Optionally ignore Touched-based tryLock unless the owner's Humanoid.MoveDirection was non-zero recently. Leave the Lockdown product (lockFor) bypass as it is.

summary: The revenge bonus for a completed robbery is skipped if the robber is currently stealing someone else's car.
evidence: onThiefHit (TheftService.luau:1465-1474) returns early whenever byThief[target] exists, even when the attacker is not that theft's victim. The recentRobbers check (1475-1482) is never reached, and the entry is not consumed.
failureScenario: A robbed B 2 minutes ago. B finds A stealing C's car and bonks A. B gets no 'REVENGE!' bonus, at exactly the dramatic moment the feature is meant for.
suggestedFix: Inside the active-theft branch, only return after handling that theft's victim case. Otherwise fall through to the recentRobbers check.
verifyReason: Confirmed. In onThiefHit, `local theft = byThief[target]; if theft and not theft.finished then ... return end` returns even when the attacker is not that theft's victim, so the recentRobbers branch is skipped. The entry is not consumed, though, so B still gets revenge with a later hit within REVENGE_WINDOW (300s) once A's current theft ends. The bonus is delayed or missed at the dramatic moment, not lost for good.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau onThiefHit: inside the active-theft branch, after updating lastHitAt and lastHitBy, return only if the attacker == theft.victim case was handled, i.e. `if attacker == theft.victim then if not theft.revengePaid then ... end return end`. Otherwise fall through to the recentRobbers check. Add a theft.spec case: A robbed B, then A is stealing from C, then B bonks A and gets paid once.

summary: The CarStolenAlert banner (y=84, 92 tall) sits on the same top-centre strip as EventsClient's pill row (y=78) and the Hot Drop banner, so during a Hot Drop or Rush Hour the victim's alarm text is covered or covers them.
evidence: NotificationController.luau:58 ALERT_BANNER_POSITION = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 84); 1306-1313 Size 660x92 in HC_Banners. EventsClient.luau:184 places the pill row at UDim2.new(0.5,0,0,78). The HUD integration doc says the Hot Drop banner uses y=128-246.
failureScenario: A theft starts during a Hot Drop countdown. The red alarm banner and the Hot Drop banner overlap, and the theft text is unreadable on phones.
suggestedFix: Move the theft banner below the event strip (e.g. y=250), or hide or shift the EventsHUD while NotificationController.isAlertActive() is true.
verifyReason: Overlap confirmed, but the effect is the reverse of the claim. Both ScreenGuis use Kit.screen (IgnoreGuiInset=false, same UIScale). The theft banner is 660x92 at y=84 (84-176) in HC_Banners, and EventsHUD's Top frame is at y=78 with the pill row at 78-118 and the Hot Drop banner at 128-246. HC_Banners has DisplayOrder Theme.Layers.Banners=30 and EventsHUD has HUD+1=11, so the theft alarm draws on top and stays readable. What gets covered is the event pills and the top of the Hot Drop banner (title and timer) while a theft alert is active.
fix: src/client/Controllers/EventsClient.luau: while NotificationController.isAlertActive() is true (lazy require, checked in the existing render or update loop), offset the 'Top' frame down by ~104 design px (to y≈182), and restore it when the alert ends. Alternatively hide the pill row during the alert. Do not move the theft banner lower, because the centre Announce banner sits at 45% height.

summary: Stealing from the Dealership always beats buying, and steal → deliver → sell is a near-free money printer.
evidence: DealershipService.luau:723-796: onSteal hands over the car for free with a flat +2★ (777, Police.luau:27), whatever its rarity. The pad refills 30s later (DealershipService.luau:39 PAD_RESTOCK=30). GarageService.luau:1094-1116 stores the stolen car as an ordinary SlotRecord with no record of where it came from. sellSlot (GarageService.luau:848-881) pays EconomyMath.sellValue = 50% of catalog price × mutation (EconomyMath.luau sellValue, Economy.luau:8). The 2★ can be cleared for $500 at a Spray Shop (Economy.luau:125, WantedService.luau:554). Two cops chase at 0.9×118 = 106 studs/s (PoliceService.luau:108), slower than every Epic/Legendary on the floor.
failureScenario: A fresh player walks into the showroom, holds F for 5.6s on a Legendary gold_rush ($300k), outruns the 106-stud/s cops in a 150-stud/s car (or pays $500 to spray), parks it, and sells it for $150,000. The pad restocks in 30s, so they repeat. They hit the 750k rebirth after about 5 heists in minutes. 'Buy $X' is never worth pressing, and 28-day progression collapses.
suggestedFix: Make the risk scale with value. Set dealer heat to Heat.dealerSteal + tier.wantedOnSteal, so Legendary+ starts at 4★ with the helicopter. Mark dealer-stolen records `hot=true` for about 10 minutes: they cannot be sold, and chopping them pays less. Leave a stolen pad empty until the next global restock. Scale spray cost (see F4).
verifyReason: Confirmed. DealershipService.onSteal always calls addHeat with PoliceConfig.Heat.dealerSteal = 2, whatever the rarity. A dealer Mythic or Secret therefore costs less heat (2★) than the same car hotwired on the street (3★, Rarity.wantedOnSteal). GarageService delivery stores dealer Loot through storeCar with no provenance, and sellSlot pays EconomyMath.sellValue (50% of price × mutation) with no restriction. The Chop Shop pays 35% without the trip home. The dealer comment ('buy -> sell can never be profitable') only covers buy/sell, not steal/sell. Some claims are overstated. The pad refills after 30s with a fresh random roll (Legendary+ is about 3% per roll at luck 1), not the same car, so '5 Legendary heists in minutes' is wrong. bank_truck (86 studs/s) is an Epic slower than 2★ cops. Cops spawn 170-330 studs away; HQ lanes are too close to qualify. The core problem is still real: the thief picks the best of 8 visible pads (about 57% chance that at least one is Epic+), and a cheap 2★ chase makes steal→sell or steal→chop worth tens of thousands of dollars per 1-2 minute cycle for a brand-new player earning $3/s. That breaks the purpose of the Buy button and early progression.
fix: src/server/Systems/DealershipService.luau: (1) Add a helper `_stealHeat(carId) = math.max(PoliceConfig.Heat.dealerSteal, tier.wantedOnSteal + 1)` (Rare/Epic 2★, Legendary 3★, Mythic/Secret 4★ + heli). Use it in onSteal's addHeat and in the StealPrompt ObjectText in attachPrompts, which currently prints Heat.dealerSteal. (2) In clearPad, when status == "stolen", set pad.restockAt = nextGlobal instead of _padRestockAt(now, nextGlobal), so a robbed pad stays empty until the 240s global restock. Sold pads keep the 30s refill. Optional design follow-up: store `hot = os.time()` on dealer-stolen SlotRecords (GarageService delivery path, car.data.source == "dealer") and block sellSlot for about 10 min.

summary: The game tells wanted players to 'hit a 🎨 Spray Shop', but nothing in the world, HUD or waypoints shows where the only two booths are.
evidence: WantedService.luau:279 shows the hint. Only EventService.luau:657, TheftService.luau:552-597 and DealershipService.luau:595/878 ever fire Waypoint; none of them targets a spray booth. WaypointController.luau:125-128 even has 🎨/🔧 icons for 'spray'/'chop' ids that nothing ever sets. There is no minimap anywhere in src. There are only 2 booths (MapLayout.luau:193-201) on a 1600×1600-stud grid.
failureScenario: A mobile player gets their first 1★ from a carjack, reads the toast, and has no idea where a Spray Shop is. They drive around aimlessly with cops on them until busted. This breaks pillar 6 (no reading, icons over text) and one of the three escape routes in the core loop.
suggestedFix: In WaypointController, add an auto waypoint 'spray' to the nearest MapLayout.sprayZones() booth while the Wanted attribute is > 0, labelled '🎨 SPRAY $<cost>'. Hide it when Wanted is 0. Optionally pulse the booth's neon sign for wanted players.
verifyReason: Confirmed. WantedService.applyStars shows '🚨 Cops are on you! Break line of sight or hit a 🎨 Spray Shop.' on the first wanted level. The only Waypoint senders are EventService (hotdrop clear), TheftService and DealershipService. WaypointController's auto waypoints are only 'home' and 'hotdrop'; iconFor has a 🎨 'spray' branch that nothing uses. No client file references spray zones, and there is no minimap. The booth's only marker is a 24×6 SurfaceGui 'SPRAY' sign about 23 studs up, facing one road. Severity is lowered from high because line-of-sight decay is still a working escape, so this is a discoverability gap and not a broken loop.
fix: src/client/Controllers/WaypointController.luau: add `updateAutoSpray()` to the AUTO_TICK block next to updateAutoHome(). When player:GetAttribute("Wanted") > 0, pick the MapLayout.sprayZones() entry nearest the character (aim at zone.cframe.Position minus size.Y/2) and call setAuto("spray", pos, color, `SPRAY {Format.cash(Economy.SPRAY_COST_PER_STAR * stars)}`). Otherwise call clearAuto("spray"). The existing iconFor gives it 🎨.

summary: Resetting the character while wanted is a free escape: it teleports the player into their safe-house garage with no bust penalty, bypassing the 'can't Go Home while wanted' rule.
evidence: PlotService.luau:1456-1463 moves every new character to OWNER_SPAWN. PlotService.luau:1479-1482 blocks the GoHome remote while wanted. PoliceService.luau:696 treats the inside of your own garage as safe: no bust, never 'seen'. WantedService has no Died or CharacterAdded handling, so stars persist and decay unseen (592-609). The cash penalty only happens in bust() (460-508).
failureScenario: A 4★ player is boxed in with BustProgress at 0.8. They press Esc → Reset and respawn inside their own garage, where they are untouchable and unseen. The stars decay and they keep 100% of their cash. They can also farm the escape/escape3 contracts this way.
suggestedFix: In WantedService, hook Humanoid.Died (or CharacterRemoving) while stars > 0 and treat it as a bust: take the penalty, clear the stars, and respawn at Police HQ (PlotService should skip moving the character home for busted players). Also call StarterGui:SetCore('ResetButtonCallback', false) on the client while Wanted > 0.
verifyReason: Confirmed. No server code handles Humanoid.Died or CharacterRemoving for wanted players, and the client never disables the reset button (no SetCore anywhere). While the character is dead, PoliceService.updateSuspectInfo marks st.valid = false, and bustPass requires st.valid, so the bust cannot finish. PlotService.onCharacter calls moveCharacterHome on every spawn without checking Wanted. In the garage st.safe = true, so isSeen is false: the stars decay, the cops wait outside, and the cash penalty in bust() never applies. The car itself is still effectively lost because it is left abandoned. So the exploit skips the cash penalty, the busted stat and the BUSTED moment, not the car loss. That makes it medium, not high. Contract farming is not unique to reset, since driving or walking home while wanted is already a safe zone.
fix: src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau: in onPlayerAdded, connect CharacterAdded and then the Humanoid's Died event. If stars > 0 and the player is not busting, call WantedService.bust(player) (penalty, stars cleared, Busted fired) and set st.respawnAtHQ = true. Expose `WantedService.consumeRespawnAtHQ(player): boolean`. src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau onCharacter: lazily require WantedService. If consumeRespawnAtHQ(player) is true, PivotTo MapLayout.bustedReleaseCFrame() instead of moveCharacterHome. src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau: on the Wanted attribute change, pcall StarterGui:SetCore("ResetButtonCallback", stars == 0) as a UX deterrent. The server hook is still required because clients can kill their own humanoid.

summary: Spray cost is a flat $250 per star and works even with cops touching the car. That is unaffordable for new players (whom the hint sends there) and trivial for everyone else.
evidence: Economy.luau:125 SPRAY_COST_PER_STAR = 250. Economy.luau STARTING_CASH = 150. WantedService.luau:541-578 has no isSeen or proximity check; it just spends and clears (554, 569). WantedService.luau:279 recommends spraying on the first wanted level.
failureScenario: Early game: a new player's first 1★ costs $250 against $150 on hand, so the recommended action fails with an error toast (562-565). Mid game: a player earning $900/s clears 5★ for $1,250 (about 1.4s of income) while six cruisers sit on their bumper. Chases stop mattering (pillar 3).
suggestedFix: Use cost = max(100×stars, incomePerSec × 8 × stars). Require PoliceService.isSeen(player) == false, or a 2.5s 'spraying' stop inside the booth during which bustPass still runs. Show the cost on the spray waypoint.
verifyReason: Confirmed. onSprayAttempt charges SPRAY_COST_PER_STAR (250) × stars with no isSeen or proximity check. VehicleService.zonePass fires SprayAttempt on zone entry at any speed, so driving through clears even five stars while cruisers are on the bumper. For mid-game income ($900/s), $1,250 is trivial. The early-game half is overstated. The first wanted level usually comes after Rare+ steals or carjacks, when the player already has more than $250 (and brand-new heat is halved). Still, a fresh player can face the 'Get some cash first!' toast. Note that SprayAttempt fires only on entry, so a refused spray needs the player to leave the zone and come back.
fix: src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau onSprayAttempt: (1) Before charging, if isSeen(player) then rate-limit notify '🚔 They're watching! Lose them, then spray' and return without charging or setting lastSprayAt. (2) cost = math.max(Economy.SPRAY_COST_PER_STAR, math.floor(getIncome(player) * Economy.SPRAY_INCOME_SECONDS)) * st.stars. src/shared/Config/Economy.luau: add SPRAY_INCOME_SECONDS = 8 and lower SPRAY_COST_PER_STAR to about 100. Optional: in src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau zonePass, re-fire SprayAttempt about every 1s while the car stays in the zone, so an unseen player who waits inside gets sprayed.

summary: Police top speed is capped at 118 × ≤1.08 and the helicopter at 95, so any Legendary+ car (150-175) outruns every chase. Hot Drop and 5★ chases are not a threat.
evidence: PoliceService.luau:108 SPEED_MULT_BY_STARS max 1.08, applied at 1867-1873. Cars.luau:639 police topSpeed = 118. Cars.luau:409-495: Legendary/Mythic top speeds are 150-175. Police nitro is only 3s and only below 10° off-nose (1274-1276). rubberBand teleports cops 250-340 studs BEHIND, out of view (863-875). HELI_MAX_SPEED = 95 (line 113). Hot drops are always Legendary+ (Events.luau HOT_DROP_RARITY) with only 3★ (Police.luau:29).
failureScenario: The Hot Drop claimer gets a rocket_car (175 studs/s) and 3★. They drive straight down the ring road for about 40s; cops at about 114 never close the gap, the stars decay, and the server's signature 'everyone rush over' moment ends with no chase worth clipping.
suggestedFix: Scale each unit's SpeedMultiplier by the suspect car: mult = max(starMult, suspectTop/118 × (0.8 + 0.05×stars)). Let rubber-band spawns go AHEAD of fast suspects (interceptors). Add 3★ spike strips and 4★ roadblocks (listed as not built). Make the helicopter's top speed at least the suspect's.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Police topSpeed is 118 and SPEED_MULT_BY_STARS tops out at 1.08, plus CATCHUP_BONUS 0.12 only when far behind with no line of sight (at most about 141). Police nitro only fires at 4★+, under 10° off-nose and more than 120 studs away. HELI_MAX_SPEED is 95. rubberBand and spawns place units behind the suspect at SIGHT_RANGE+30..+120, which is out of sight, so decay keeps running. Legendary/Mythic cars run 150-175 (mini_tank at 78 is the exception), and hot drops are Legendary+ with 3★, so a straight run escapes. This is partly intentional: the comments say 'fast cars (and nitro) can outrun the chopper'. But it contradicts '5-star cops are relentless' and the hot drop's purpose as a showpiece chase.
fix: src/server/Systems/PoliceService.luau only. In updateSuspectInfo, when driving, set st.topSpeed from Cars.get(car.carId).topSpeed (0 on foot). In maintainUnit, use mult = math.max(base, (st.topSpeed / Cars.Police.topSpeed) * (0.8 + 0.05 * stars)) + (farBehind and CATCHUP_BONUS or 0). The VehicleController clamp of 3 is fine. In updateHeli, clamp desiredVel to math.max(HELI_MAX_SPEED, st.topSpeed * 0.9). Optional: in rubberBand, when the suspect's flat speed is above about 120, pass `ahead` candidates (rotate the behind vector 180°) so fast suspects meet interceptors.

summary: WantedSeen (whether cops can currently see you) is computed and replicated, but no client reads it, so players get no feedback that they are escaping.
evidence: WantedService.luau:597-601 sets the WantedSeen attribute every decay pass. A grep of src/client finds no reader. HUDController.luau:1759-1776 flashes the stars red/blue whenever stars > 0, whether or not the player is seen, and refreshStars (1074-1128) ignores visibility. There is also no decay timer attribute.
failureScenario: The player broke line of sight 20s ago and is 5s from losing a star, but the HUD looks exactly as it does when a cruiser is on their bumper. The player can't learn the hide mechanic and assumes only spraying works.
suggestedFix: In HUDController, listen to WantedSeen and, while it is false, dim/blink the stars GTA-style and stop the police-light stroke. Add a WantedDecayAt server-time attribute in WantedService and draw a small ring counting down to the next star loss.
verifyReason: Confirmed. WantedService._decayPass writes the WantedSeen attribute, and the header says the HUD should flash the stars while the player is hidden. A grep of src/client finds no WantedSeen reader. HUDController.animateTick flashes the police stroke whenever stars > 0, and refreshStars ignores visibility. No attribute exposes the decay timer. This is an integration gap that hides the main escape mechanic. Polish rather than broken logic, but it directly affects learnability.
fix: src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau: listen to GetAttributeChangedSignal("WantedSeen") and cache it. In animateTick, when stars > 0 and not seen, blink the filled stars (alternate TextTransparency 0/0.6 at about 3 Hz) and set the stroke to Theme.Colors.Stroke instead of the red/blue flash. Restore both when seen. Optional: in src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau _decayPass, also set a `WantedDecayAt` attribute (Workspace:GetServerTimeNow() + (st.nextDecayAt - now)) while unseen, for a countdown ring.

summary: Hot Drops land anchored in the middle of intersections. Traffic stops, then ghosts into the car and piles up as abandoned Loot, and police turn waypoints aim straight at the anchored car.
evidence: Map.luau:82-93: every HotDropPoint is a multiple of 160, i.e. an intersection center. EventService.luau:910 spawns it anchored. TrafficService.luau:966-973 sees it as a 'static' blocker. At 1050-1057, after 8s with a player within 150 studs (always true at a hot drop), the car ghosts and drives into it. 1104-1106 then releases it as 'knocked', and 705-711 turns it into unowned Loot. That Loot only despawns when nobody is within 120 studs (VehicleService.luau:1652-1659). PoliceService.bestJunction (386-415) routes through intersection centers.
failureScenario: During the 3-minute live phase, crossing traffic piles into the hot drop. Racing players crash into the anchored car and the junk around it. Cops chasing anyone through that junction steer into it and take crash damage.
suggestedFix: Move HotDropPoints to off-lane spots (block-edge lots or plazas next to a curb cut). During the countdown, despawn or reroute traffic within 40 studs of the beacon. Never let traffic ghost into anchored or non-traffic obstacles.
verifyReason: Mostly confirmed. All 10 Map.HotDropPoints are multiples of 160, which are intersection centers, and the car is anchored there for up to 180s. TrafficService.scanPass classifies any non-player, non-traffic vehicle as 'static'. After STATIC_GIVEUP (8s), with a player within 150 studs (always true at a hot drop), the car ghosts. Ghost only skips the limiter and does not turn off collisions, so the AlignPosition (10g) pushes into the anchored car until the carrot is more than 25 studs away. It is then released as 'knocked' and becomes an unowned Loot car anyone can Drive with zero hold. PoliceService._nextWaypoint aims turns at the exact intersection center. Straight-through traffic in the ±8 lanes mostly passes outside the 6-stud cone, so mainly left-turners get stuck. The effect is a few junk cars and cop bumps at one junction during a ≤3 min window, so severity is low.
fix: src/server/Systems/TrafficService.luau scanPass: tag obstacles whose car.kind is "HotDrop" or "Police" (or whose chassis is Anchored) as blocker "hard". For "hard" blockers never set ghostUntil. After STATIC_GIVEUP, destroy the traffic car when no player is within about 150 studs, otherwise keep waiting. This also fixes F12. Optional: src/shared/Config/Map.luau, move HotDropPoints off the exact intersection centers (for example into plaza or lot spots next to a curb cut).

summary: Carjack heat ignores rarity: a Mythic taken from traffic gives 1★, but the same car hotwired while parked gives 3★.
evidence: TrafficService.luau:753 always uses PoliceConfig.Heat.carjack = 1 (Police.luau:26). StreetSpawnService.luau:254 and VehicleService.luau:1198 use tier.wantedOnSteal (Rarity.luau:80/90/100 give 2/3/3). SPEC §2.5 says 'wanted stars rise with rarity'.
failureScenario: Players learn to carjack only Legendary/Mythic traffic. That gets 1 slow cop (0.82×) instead of 3 cops, so the rarest cars in the city become the lowest-risk steals.
suggestedFix: Use heat = math.max(Heat.carjack, tier.wantedOnSteal) in onCarjack (optionally +1 for the violence).
verifyReason: Confirmed. TrafficService.onCarjack calls VehicleService.addStealHeat(player, PoliceConfig.Heat.carjack = 1). Traffic rolls use the same streetWeight table (Rolls.car("street")), so Legendary and Mythic traffic exists and churns often. Parked steals (StreetSpawnService.onStolen) and Loot hotwires use tier.wantedOnSteal (Legendary 2, Mythic 3). Carjack hold is also shorter (×0.9). The rarest cars are therefore the lowest-risk steals when taken from traffic. The code follows SPEC §6 TrafficService ('wanted + Heat.carjack'), but that line conflicts with SPEC §2.5 ('wanted stars rise with rarity').
fix: src/server/Systems/TrafficService.luau onCarjack: `local tier = Rarity.Tiers[car.rarity] or Rarity.Tiers.Common; local heat = VehicleService.addStealHeat(player, math.max(PoliceConfig.Heat.carjack, tier.wantedOnSteal), "carjack")`. Rarity is already required at line 30. Update the SPEC §6 TrafficService line to match.

summary: The Rebirth menu advertises '+10% rare car luck per rebirth', but REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS is never applied to any roll.
evidence: Economy.luau:120 defines REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS. MenuController.luau:2737 displays it. A grep of src/server finds no reference. Every roll uses EventService.getLuck(), which is server-wide (EventService.luau:112-121, 523-525): TrafficService.luau:785, StreetSpawnService.luau:96-102, DealershipService.luau:540-546.
failureScenario: A player rebirths partly for luck, but their odds of finding rare cars are unchanged. The menu shows a promise the game doesn't keep.
suggestedFix: Street, traffic and dealer stock are shared across players, so either remove the line, or turn the bonus into something per-player (e.g. hotwire speed, or extra luck on that player's daily/playtime car rewards via Rolls.rarity).
verifyReason: Confirmed, and a duplicate of the earlier REBIRTH-LUCK-NOT-APPLIED finding (docs/integration/findings_contracts.json), which is still unfixed. Economy.REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS is read only by MenuController:2737 ('+10% rare car luck'). Every roll uses the server-wide EventService.getLuck(). Income, the main rebirth reward, works, so this is low, not medium.
fix: src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau:2737: drop the '🍀 +X% rare car luck' segment, leaving '🔒 +10s garage lock (every rebirth)'. Remove '(and luck)' from the src/server/Systems/RebirthService.luau header and remove or comment out Economy.REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS. Applying real per-player luck would be a design change, because street, traffic and dealer stock are shared.

summary: The Chop Shop and Cash Rain have no waypoint. 'Chop it at the Chop Shop' is a dead end, and the 45s Cash Rain is over before players find the plaza.
evidence: GarageService.luau:1106 and DealershipService.luau:785 tell the player to chop the car, but give no location (the Chop Shop is in the far corner block (-5,-5), Map.luau Blocks). EventService.luau:1174-1180 only Announces Cash Rain. CASH_RAIN_DURATION is 45 (Events.luau). Players spawn in their garages, not at the 'Spawn Plaza' (PlotService.luau:1456-1463). EventsClient only shows a pill.
failureScenario: The player arrives home with a full garage and is told to chop the car, but has no idea where the Chop Shop is. When Cash Rain fires, players who have never been to the plaza can't find it in 45s.
suggestedFix: Fire Waypoint('chop', chopZone position, …) when a delivery fails with 'full', and also on dealer steal / hot drop claim with a full garage. In EventsClient, set waypoint 'cashrain' to MapLayout.poiCenter('SpawnPlaza') while eventState.cashRain is active.
verifyReason: Confirmed. The GarageService delivery 'full' branch and the DealershipService steal path only send text toasts naming the Chop Shop, which is in the far corner block (-5,-5). EventService.startCashRain only Announces and posts to the feed. EventsClient shows a 'CASH RAIN @ PLAZA' pill with no waypoint, and players spawn in their garages. The impact is smaller than claimed. A full garage can be fixed on the spot by selling a car, and re-entering the Loot car in the drop-off retries delivery. The plaza is central and next to the Dealership the tutorial points to, so this is low.
fix: src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau delivery 'full' branch, inside the existing fullNotifyAt rate-limit: `local cf = MapLayout.chopZone(); Net.fireClient("Waypoint", player, "chop", cf.Position - Vector3.new(0, 7, 0), Color3.fromRGB(255,140,40), "CHOP SHOP")`. Clear it on the next successful delivery or chop. src/client/Controllers/EventsClient.luau: while the event state has cashRain active, call WaypointController.set("cashrain", MapLayout.poiCenter("SpawnPlaza"), Theme.Colors.Cash, "💰 CASH RAIN"), and clear it when the state ends.

summary: Common and Uncommon street steals give 0★. That is about 86% of street cars, so most steals have no getaway, against pillar 1 ('Every steal is a getaway').
evidence: Rarity.luau:40 and 50: wantedOnSteal = 0 for Common/Uncommon, with streetWeight 60/26 (37, 47) out of about 100. StreetSpawnService.luau:254 adds tier.wantedOnSteal.
failureScenario: After the tutorial, most hotwires are a quiet drive home. The chase loop only starts with Rare+ cars, which are about 14% of spawns, so the game's differentiator rarely shows up.
suggestedFix: Uncommon → 1★. For Common, after the player's first delivery, roll a 35% 'witness' chance of 1★ (keep the free first steal).
verifyReason: The facts are confirmed. Rarity.luau gives Common and Uncommon wantedOnSteal = 0, with streetWeight 60 and 26 out of about 100, so about 86% of street hotwires (at luck 1) have no chase. This is a deliberate config value, but it conflicts with pillar 1 ('Every steal is a getaway… the differentiator') and SPEC §2.2 'First steal: no wanted level', which implies later steals do add heat. VehicleService's isFirstSteal/freeStealUsed only matters for parked cars if Commons add heat. It is a tuning call, not a code bug. Note that 1★ cops (about 97 studs/s) outpace all Common/Uncommon cars (66-92), so blanket 1★ on Commons would raise newbie busts.
fix: Minimal: src/shared/Config/Rarity.luau, Uncommon.wantedOnSteal = 1. Optional for Commons, in src/server/Systems/StreetSpawnService.luau onStolen: if tier.id == "Common" and the player has tutorialDone and is not on a first steal, then with rng:NextNumber() < 0.35 use heat 1 ('witness'). Keep the first and tutorial steal free.

summary: Traffic treats police cruisers as 'static' obstacles and ghosts into them after 8s, shoving cops that are boxing in a suspect.
evidence: TrafficService.luau:966-973: a police car has driver == nil and no entry, so isPlayerCar = false and isTraffic = false, which makes it 'static'. At 1050-1057, after STATIC_GIVEUP with a player within 150 studs, the traffic car ghosts and drives through, held by an AlignPosition with 10g MaxForce (844). PoliceService.luau:1200-1205: the box-in parks cops in the lane around a slow suspect.
failureScenario: A suspect stalls in a lane and cops box them in. 8s later a traffic car ploughs through the cops, pushing them out of the 16-stud bust radius or flinging the suspect, so the bust timer resets.
suggestedFix: Give Police (and anchored HotDrop cars) their own blocker kind that never ghosts. Despawn the waiting traffic car when it is out of view, or reroute it at the next junction.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Police units have car.driver == nil and no traffic entry, so scanPass labels them 'static'. After STATIC_GIVEUP (8s) near players, the traffic car ghosts. Ghost only bypasses the limiter, not collision, and the AlignPosition (MaxForce = mass×g×10) shoves whatever is in the way. The scenario is narrow. A boxed-in suspect who stays slow inside the 16-stud bust radius is busted in 2.5s, well before the 8s give-up, so this mostly affects cops parked outside a garage door or holding position, not live busts.
fix: Same change as F7 in src/server/Systems/TrafficService.luau scanPass: treat car.kind == "Police" (and HotDrop or anchored chassis) as a non-ghostable blocker. On give-up, destroy the traffic car if no player is within view radius, otherwise keep waiting.

summary: Cops that are leaving (stars dropped to 0) still flash and wail, so players think they are still being chased.
evidence: PoliceService.luau:752 sets Siren = false on sendAway. EffectsController.luau:1465-1513 flashes every Police-tagged model within 300 studs, and SoundController.luau:619-633 gives siren slots to the nearest Police-tagged models. Neither reads 'Siren'.
failureScenario: The player gets 'ESCAPED!', but the departing cruisers next to them keep screaming for up to 15s and the feedback contradicts itself.
suggestedFix: Skip models with GetAttribute('Siren') == false in both controllers, and refresh on AttributeChanged.
verifyReason: Confirmed, and a duplicate of the earlier POLICE-SIREN-ATTR-IGNORED finding, still unfixed. PoliceService sets Siren=false in sendAway and markWrecked. EffectsController.updateSirens flashes every tracked Police model within SIREN_RANGE, and SoundController gives siren slots to the nearest Police models. Neither reads 'Siren'. Leaving units live up to LEAVE_TIME + LEAVE_MAX_TIME = 15s.
fix: src/client/Controllers/EffectsController.luau updateSirens: if model:GetAttribute("Siren") == false, turn rec.light off, reset the red/blue part transparency once, and `continue`. src/client/Controllers/SoundController.luau siren candidate loop: skip models whose Siren attribute == false. Both run every tick, so no AttributeChanged hook is needed.

summary: The result of VehicleService.seat is ignored in the carjack, hot drop claim and dealer steal. Heat, stats and contract credit are applied even when the player never got in.
evidence: VehicleService.seat returns (false, reason) without throwing (894-976). TrafficService.luau:748 ignores it. EventService.luau:750: call() returns pcall-ok, so `seated` is true even when the seat fails. DealershipService.luau:773 does the same. Heat is then added at TrafficService.luau:753, EventService.luau:755 and DealershipService.luau:777.
failureScenario: The claimer dies or is knocked down right as the 5s hold completes. The hot drop is marked claimed, they get +3★, stats.hotDrops +1 and the contract credit, and the car sits as unclaimed Loot that anyone can hotwire.
suggestedFix: Read seat's second return value (e.g. local _, ok = call(...); ok = ok == true). On failure, skip the heat/stats/contract and leave the car claimable (for hot drops, restore the HotDrop kind and the prompt).
verifyReason: Confirmed, and a duplicate of the earlier seat-result-misread / BUG-1 findings, still unfixed. EventService.call and DealershipService.call return (pcallOk, result), and `local seated = call(...)` keeps only pcallOk. TrafficService.onCarjack ignores VehicleService.seat's (false, reason). In practice seat rarely fails here. canClaim and canCarjack already reject stunned players, the client disables prompts while stunned, and there is no ordinary death. So this is a theoretical race, low.
fix: src/server/Systems/EventService.luau claimHotDrop: `local okCall, res = call("VehicleService","seat",car,player); if not (okCall and res == true) then hd.claimed = false; setKind(car,"HotDrop"); car.chassis.Anchored = true; addClaimPrompt(hd); return end` before heat, stats and contracts. src/server/Systems/DealershipService.luau onSteal: `local okCall, seated = call(...)`; if seated ~= true, skip addHeat and progress (the car stays as unowned Loot). src/server/Systems/TrafficService.luau onCarjack: `if not VehicleService.seat(car, player) then return end` before addStealHeat and contractProgress.

summary: A Hot Drop can be claimed with a full garage, and the player only finds out when they reach their drop-off.
evidence: EventService.luau:709-731: canClaim never checks GarageService.freeSlots. A dealer steal warns at steal time (DealershipService.luau:783-786). The error only appears at delivery (GarageService.luau:1100-1109).
failureScenario: The player wins the hot drop race, survives a 3★ chase home, and is told 'Garage full!'. Selling a car means getting out, which stops the delivery retries.
suggestedFix: On claim, if freeSlots == 0, Notify 'Garage full – sell a car or chop this one' and set the chop waypoint (F10).
verifyReason: Confirmed. EventService.canClaim never checks GarageService.freeSlots, and the only full-garage message is at delivery. The claim that selling 'stops the delivery retries' is wrong. setDriver resets st.inDropoff, so re-entering the Loot car in the drop-off fires DeliveryAttempt again, and the player is safe inside their own garage while selling. Low.
fix: src/server/Systems/EventService.luau claimHotDrop, after a successful seat: `local _, free = call("GarageService","freeSlots",player); if typeof(free) == "number" and free <= 0 then Net.fireClient("Notify", player, "info", "📦 Garage full: sell a car first, or chop this one at the Chop Shop!") end`. Optionally also fire the chop waypoint from F10. Do not block the claim.

summary: The drop-in teleports an anchored car through whatever is standing on the landing spot. The spot is only checked for blocking when the drop is scheduled, 20s before the car lands.
evidence: EventService.luau:977-979: isPointBlocked is only used when picking the point. dropIn (842-857) PivotTo's the anchored model every Heartbeat, and the car is spawned and moved at 929-930 with no re-check after the 20s countdown, while EventsClient tells players 'YOU'RE HERE!'.
failureScenario: Players and their cars crowd the beacon center, and the Legendary is teleported into them. Characters and cars get flung, and traffic that drove into the spot during the countdown ends up overlapping the car.
suggestedFix: Before spawning, re-run isPointBlocked and clear players and unoccupied cars within about 10 studs (push them outward), or land on a cleared pad at the ring edge.
verifyReason: Confirmed. isPointBlocked runs only in startHotDrop when the point is chosen. After the 20s countdown, runHotDrop spawns and anchors the car and dropIn PivotTo's it down over 0.9s with no re-check of vehicles or characters. EventsClient tells players within 30 studs 'YOU'RE HERE!', which draws them onto the landing spot.
fix: src/server/Systems/EventService.luau runHotDrop, just before V.spawn: for each player whose HumanoidRootPart is within 10 studs of hd.position (and not seated), PivotTo it outward to about 14 studs. For VehicleService.all() cars within 16 studs that have no driver and kind Traffic or Loot, release or destroy them (TrafficService.release + VehicleService.destroy(car, "cleared")). Leave player-driven cars alone.

summary: The 'Lose the Cops' product takes Robux even when the player has 0 stars.
evidence: MonetizationService.luau:341-349: the handler returns true whenever the pcall succeeds. WantedService.clear (349-355) silently does nothing at 0 stars. MenuController does not gate clear_wanted on the Wanted attribute.
failureScenario: Once the product ids are set, a player who buys it after the stars have already decayed (or during the bust grace) is charged for nothing.
suggestedFix: Return false from the handler when WantedService.getStars(player) == 0, so the receipt stays NotProcessedYet. Disable the Store button when Wanted == 0.
verifyReason: Confirmed, and a duplicate of the earlier CLEAR-WANTED-NOOP-PURCHASE finding. The clear_wanted handler returns true whenever callSystem doesn't throw. WantedService.clear silently returns at 0 stars, and MenuController doesn't gate the button. The bug is latent: every product id in Monetization.luau is 0 and the Store hides id-0 items. Low.
fix: src/server/Systems/MonetizationService.luau clear_wanted handler: `local okS, stars = callSystem("WantedService","getStars",player); if not okS or typeof(stars) ~= "number" or stars <= 0 then return false end` before clearing. src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau: disable or grey the clear_wanted buy button while player:GetAttribute("Wanted") == 0. Because NotProcessedYet is re-offered on later receipts, consider storing a pending credit on data instead of returning false forever.

summary: Internal reason codes ('gone', 'stunned', 'loading') are shown to players as error toasts.
evidence: EventService.luau:711, 715, 718 and 722 return these codes from canClaim. VehicleService.luau:1097-1100 sends any non-empty reason as a Notify error.
failureScenario: A player whose claim races the expiry, a stun, or their data load sees a red toast that just says 'gone' or 'loading'.
suggestedFix: Return nil for silent refusals, or friendly text ('Too late – someone grabbed it!').
verifyReason: Confirmed. addClaimPrompt goes through VehicleService.addStealPrompt with canSteal = canClaim. VehicleService notifies any non-empty reason as an error, so 'gone', 'stunned' and 'loading' would show as raw toasts. These are rare races: prompts are destroyed after a claim, the client disables prompts while stunned, and loading only happens right after joining.
fix: src/server/Systems/EventService.luau canClaim: return `false, nil` for the 'gone' and 'stunned' cases and `false, "Still loading. Try again in a sec!"` for 'loading'. Keep the friendly 'Get out of your car first!'.

summary: The BUSTED overlay only shows the cash lost. Losing the car, often the most valuable thing, is never explained.
evidence: WantedService.luau:422-427 destroys a Loot car (or fails the theft for a Stolen one), but the Busted payload is only lostCash (488). HUDController.showBusted(lostCash) has no car field.
failureScenario: A busted player loses a Mythic hot drop. The stamp says '-$1,200', and they don't understand where their car went (pillar 4 promises 'impound').
suggestedFix: Send the car label in the Busted payload (e.g. Busted(lost, carLabel)) and show '🚗 <car> IMPOUNDED' under the stamp.
verifyReason: Confirmed. WantedService.handleCar destroys a Loot car (or fails a Stolen theft), but bust() fires Busted with only `lost`. HUDController's listener and showBusted(lostCash) take only the cash amount.
fix: src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau: have handleCar return a label (car.carId and car.mutation, formatted as in other services) when it destroyed Loot or failed a theft. In bust(), send `hooks.fireClient("Busted", player, lost, carLabel)`. src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau: extend the listener and showBusted(lostCash, carLabel?) to add a '🚗 <car> IMPOUNDED' line under the stamp. Update the Remotes.luau comment.

summary: Spraying overwrites the color of mutated cars, so a Gold, Diamond or Galaxy car looks like it lost its mutation.
evidence: WantedService.luau:519-539 sets d.Color on Paint='primary' parts directly. The CarBuilder.repaint(model, color) helper, which re-applies the mutation, exists (vehicles-world doc) but isn't used.
failureScenario: A player sprays a GALAXY car, it turns flat pink, and they assume the spray destroyed the mutation (the stored record is fine, but the feedback is wrong).
suggestedFix: Call CarBuilder.repaint(car.model, color), or skip recoloring when the Mutation attribute isn't 'None' (change the accent only).
verifyReason: Confirmed. WantedService._repaint writes d.Color directly on Paint='primary' parts. That overrides Gold, Diamond and Galaxy colors while keeping their material. Rainbow is unaffected because WheelAnimator cycles it client-side. CarBuilder.repaint(model, color) exists: it sets BaseColor and re-applies the mutation, and is tested in carbuilder.spec ('repaint keeps mutation'). The stored record is fine, and the display car rebuilt on delivery looks correct.
fix: src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau _repaint: lazily require ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Vehicle.CarBuilder (pcall). If available, call CarBuilder.repaint(model, color) instead of the manual loop, and fall back to the existing loop only if the require fails. Keep the Health and TiresPopped resets.

summary: Rush Hour and Server Luck only affect new rolls, so the 'rare cars are everywhere' announcement barely shows on the street within the 2-minute Rush Hour.
evidence: EventService.luau:1202-1208 announces 'rare cars are everywhere!'. StreetSpawnService.luau:43: parked cars only re-roll after 300-540s untouched with nobody within 160 studs. Existing traffic keeps its rolls; only the extra Rush Hour spawns use the boosted luck.
failureScenario: Players rush out after the announcement and see the same parked cars as before.
suggestedFix: When Rush Hour or Server Luck starts, re-roll a share of out-of-view parked cars and prefer spawning the extra traffic near players.
verifyReason: Confirmed with nuance. Luck only affects new rolls (Rolls.rarity multiplies Rare+ weights). Parked cars re-roll only after LIFETIME 300-540s with nobody within 160 studs. Rush Hour adds about 80% more traffic spawned 150-450 studs from players at 2.5× luck, and despawn/respawn churn also uses the boosted luck, so some effect is visible, just weaker than the announcement suggests.
fix: src/server/Systems/StreetSpawnService.luau: add `StreetSpawnService.rerollOutOfView(fraction)`, which expires (expiresAt = 0) a share of entries with no player within ROTATE_CLEAR_RADIUS so the next tick re-rolls them with the current luck. Call it from src/server/Systems/EventService.luau startRushHour and activateServerLuck (lazy call).

summary: MapBuilder's 'RestockBoard' (tag DealerRestockBoard) is never drawn on. It is a blank dark panel behind DealershipService's own countdown sign.
evidence: MapBuilder.luau:1447-1457 builds and tags it. Nothing else in src references DealerRestockBoard. DealershipService.luau:469-470 builds a separate sign at center + (0,0,41).
failureScenario: A dead, unlabeled board sits on the showroom's back glass.
suggestedFix: Delete the MapBuilder board, or have DealershipService draw its SurfaceGui onto the tagged part instead of building a second sign.
verifyReason: Confirmed, and a duplicate of the earlier MAPBUILDER-DEALER-TAG-CONTRACT-UNUSED finding. MapBuilder builds and tags 'RestockBoard' (18×6 at z+45.2, y 8-14), and its comment says DealershipService draws on it, but nothing references the tag. DealershipService builds its own 34×10 sign at z+41 (y 9-19), so the dark board is almost fully hidden behind it, with about 1 stud showing. Cosmetic.
fix: src/server/Systems/MapBuilder.luau: delete the RestockBoard part and its DealerRestockBoard tag (around lines 1447-1457) and fix the comment. Leave DealershipService's own sign as is.

summary: There is no server settling controller for cars after the driver exits (SPEC §8). Abandoned cars rest on their bump-stops.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:841-853: setDriver(nil) only calls SetNetworkOwner(nil). No VehicleController is created server-side. The SPEC says 'server keeps controllers only for police and for cars settling after exit'. The CarBuilder known issues note that cars without a controller can tip about 11° on their centerline bump-stops.
failureScenario: A suspect bails out at speed. The car slides and tips on its belly, then is anchored after 10s of rest, which looks broken. A cop that later rams the anchored car crashes into an immovable object.
suggestedFix: Create a server VehicleController (isServer=true, zero input) for driverless unanchored cars until they are rest-anchored, then destroy it. The police path shows server stepping already works.
verifyReason: Confirmed. setDriver(nil) only hands network ownership to the server. No server code outside PoliceService creates a VehicleController, which deviates from SPEC §8 ('server keeps controllers… for cars settling after exit'). vehicles-world.md's known issues say a car resting on its centerline bump-stops without a controller tips about 11°. Cars are rest-anchored after PARK_ANCHOR_AFTER = 10s, which is spec'd behavior, so the 'immovable when rammed' part is by design. Cosmetic.
fix: src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau: in setDriver(nil), for non-Police unanchored cars, create VehicleController.new(model, car.def, { isServer = true }) with zero input and step it on PreSimulation. Destroy it when the rest-anchor code anchors the chassis (around line 1638), when a driver enters, or when the car is destroyed. Keep the lifetime bounded (for example 15s max) because server controllers replicate VectorForce writes every frame (PERF-01).

summary: The Chop Shop silently ignores Owned and Stolen cars, and destroys Loot instantly with no confirmation.
evidence: GarageService.luau:1148-1151 returns silently for non-Loot cars. VehicleService.luau:1489-1492 fires ChopAttempt the moment the car enters the zone.
failureScenario: A player drives their own car in expecting to sell it and nothing happens. A fleeing player cuts through the shop in a Mythic hot drop and it is chopped for 35% with no way back.
suggestedFix: Notify 'You can't chop your own car' for Owned/Stolen. For Loot, require a 1.5s stop in the zone, or a prompt showing the chop value.
verifyReason: Confirmed. GarageService.onChop returns silently for any kind except Loot, and zonePass fires ChopAttempt on the first tick inside the zone at any speed. The 'cuts through while fleeing' scenario is unlikely, since the zone is inside a dead-end building in the far corner block, but there is no feedback for Owned or Stolen cars and no confirmation for valuable Loot.
fix: src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau onChop: for car.kind == "Owned", rate-limit notify '🔧 That's your own ride: sell it from your garage instead'. For "Stolen", notify 'Deliver it to your garage instead!'. Optional: src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau zonePass, fire ChopAttempt only after the car has been inside the zone at flat speed under about 8 for 1.5s, tracked like st.inChop.

summary: After the BUSTED stamp the player stays free for 1.1s before the teleport to Police HQ, and can hop into another car in that window.
evidence: WantedService.luau:501-506: releaseCharacter is called after RELEASE_DELAY with no stun or freeze. releaseCharacter (430-457) then rips the player out of any seat they got into.
failureScenario: A busted player quickly holds 'Get in' on a nearby loot car. They are seated, then torn out 1.1s later, and that car is left with a stale driver until lifePass corrects it.
suggestedFix: Set the Stunned attribute (CombatService.stun) for RELEASE_DELAY during a bust, which also disables prompts client-side.
verifyReason: The window exists: bust() calls releaseCharacter after a 1.1s task.delay with no stun, and unowned Loot cars have a 0-hold 'Drive' prompt. The consequence is milder than claimed. releaseCharacter destroys the SeatWeld, so Occupant becomes nil, onOccupantChanged runs setDriver(nil) right away, and no stale driver remains. Heat can't be added during the 8s grace either. Mostly cosmetic.
fix: src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau bust(): before task.delay, lazily call CombatService.stun(player, RELEASE_DELAY + 0.3) via sys("CombatService") with pcall. This sets Stunned, and the client disables prompts and movement. Fall back to player:SetAttribute("Stunned", true/false) around the delay if CombatService is unavailable.

summary: The first Rebirth request from each player is always silently dropped because the remote's rate limit is 0.5/s.
evidence: RebirthService.luau:303-305 registers `Net.on("Rebirth", ..., 0.5)`. Net.luau:100 creates the token bucket with `tokens = perSecond` (0.5), and Net.luau:105 `if b.tokens < 1 then return false`, so the first call is rejected with no feedback. MenuController.luau:2812-2817 sends a single `Net.fire("Rebirth")` after the confirm tap, then shows 'REBIRTHING...' for PENDING_SECONDS=3 (line 75). AdminService.luau:456 calls RebirthService.rebirth directly, so admin QA and the unit tests never go through the limiter.
failureScenario: A player saves up $750K, opens REBIRTH, taps twice to confirm, sees 'REBIRTHING...' for 3s, and then nothing happens. No Notify is sent and the button resets. They have to repeat the whole double-tap (at least 1s later) for it to work. The first press of the main retention action fails in every server session.
suggestedFix: Register the handler with a rate of at least 1 (for example `end, 1)`), since `busy[player]` already blocks concurrent rebirths. Alternatively, change `Net.allow` to start the bucket at `math.max(1, perSecond)` tokens.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Net.allow (Net.luau:100-105) creates the bucket with tokens = perSecond (0.5), and the refill adds (now - last) * perSecond = 0 on the first call, so 0.5 < 1 and the call is rejected. The only caller is MenuController.luau:2817, which fires once per confirmed tap; there is no other Rebirth fire and no client retry. The button just sits in its 3s pending state with no Notify. The second attempt is always 3s or more later (it refills to 1 token), so it succeeds. Result: the first rebirth of every server session fails silently. Rebirth is the only remote registered below 1/s (all others are 1-6). The admin `rebirth` command calls RebirthService.rebirth directly, so it bypasses the limiter, which is why QA missed this. A related issue: with any rate below 0.5 the cap min(perSecond*2, ...) stays under 1 forever, so such a remote could never fire.
fix: src/server/Systems/RebirthService.luau:305: change `end, 0.5)` to `end, 1)`. busy[player] plus the cash check already stop double rebirths. Also harden src/shared/Net.luau allow(): start the bucket at `math.max(1, perSecond)` tokens and cap it at `math.max(1, perSecond * 2)`, so a fractional rate still lets the first call through and can refill to 1.

summary: Every gamepass and product id is 0 (and GROUP_ID is 0), so the Store, all pass effects and the group bonus are off at launch. Garage pads 11-12 also advertise a pass that can't be bought.
evidence: Monetization.luau:13/20/27/34/41 (passes) and 54/61/68/75/82/89 (products) are all `id = 0`. MonetizationService.luau:211 makes hasPass false for id 0. MenuController.luau:1510 `if items.comingSoon` renders 'STORE COMING SOON!'. GarageService.luau:138 sets `passOnly = not hasSlotsPass`, so pads 11-12 always show '🅿️ +2 SLOTS PASS' (GarageClient.luau:402), but the purchase prompt only appears when the pass id is non-zero (GarageClient.luau:457). Economy.luau:187 has `GROUP_ID = 0`.
failureScenario: At launch nobody can buy VIP, slots, Master Thief, Infinite Nitro, Zapper Pass, cash, Lockdown, Lose the Cops, Server Luck or the Dragster. The Store tab is a 'coming soon' card. Every player sees a gold '+2 SLOTS PASS' label on two pads that does nothing when they walk up to it.
suggestedFix: Create the passes and products on the Creator Dashboard and fill in the ids (plus GROUP_ID) as a release-checklist step. Add a server boot warning when any id is 0 in a non-Studio server. In GarageClient, only show the PassOnly label when `Monetization.Passes.slots.id ~= 0` (otherwise show a plain lock or hide the pads).
verifyReason: Partly real. Every id being 0 is an intentional, documented placeholder (Monetization.luau header; SPEC §9/§MenuController: 'hide id 0 items'). The code handles it cleanly: storeItems hides id-0 items and shows 'coming soon', hasPass returns false, and GROUP_ID 0 disables the group bonus. Filling in the ids is a release-checklist step on the Creator Dashboard, not a code bug. The one real defect: GarageService._padInfo returns passOnly = not hasSlotsPass for pads 11-12, which is always true while the slots pass id is 0. GarageClient.renderPad (around line 401) then draws the gold '🅿️ +2 SLOTS PASS' label for every viewer, even though the purchase prompt is correctly suppressed (GarageClient:457 checks id ~= 0). So two pads in every garage advertise a pass nobody can buy.
fix: src/client/Controllers/GarageClient.luau renderPad: change `if passOnly then` to `if passOnly and Monetization.Passes.slots.id ~= 0 then` (otherwise fall through to the plain 🔒 LOCKED label). Optional: in MonetizationService.start, warn once when `not RunService:IsStudio()` and any pass or product id is 0. Treat the real ids and GROUP_ID as a release-checklist item.

summary: Stealing from the dealership costs a flat 2★ for any rarity, and spraying it off costs $500. A heist is worth about $40K on average, so Buy is pointless and early progression explodes.
evidence: DealershipService.luau:777 `addHeat(player, PoliceConfig.Heat.dealerSteal, ...)` with Police.luau:27 `dealerSteal = 2`. There is no rarity term (street steals use rarity.wantedOnSteal, up to 3★ for Mythic). Economy.luau:125 `SPRAY_COST_PER_STAR = 250`. Computed from Config/Cars + Rarity dealerWeight: expected car value per dealer roll is about $40K, so selling (50%) gives about $20K and chopping (35%) about $14K. 3% of rolls are Legendary+ (a Mythic chops for $525K-875K). A new player earns $3/s, so $40K is about 3.7 hours of income. A pad restocks 30s after a theft.
