failureScenario: Within minutes of joining, players learn to rob the showroom over and over, chop or sell the cars, spray for $500, and reach rebirth ($750K) in a few heists. Buy prompts and car prices stop mattering as a cash sink, and the 'getaway' tension is gone because 2★ is trivial to lose.
suggestedFix: Base dealer-steal heat on rarity (for example `max(Heat.dealerSteal, tier.wantedOnSteal + 1)`, so Legendary+ is 4-5★). Scale the spray cost with income or with stars². Make dealer-stolen cars sell or chop for less (for example 15%, or no sell value for 10 minutes). Consider a per-player dealer-theft cooldown.
verifyReason: Confirmed. DealershipService.luau:777 adds a flat PoliceConfig.Heat.dealerSteal (2) for any car, while street steals use tier.wantedOnSteal (Mythic/Secret 3). The SPEC states the flat value, but this breaks the 'wanted stars rise with rarity' pillar. The dealer has much higher Legendary+/Secret weights, 8 pads to pick from, a 30s pad restock, no per-player cooldown and no rarity-scaled heat. onChop has no wanted check, so a thief can chop while still chased. The economics are overstated, though. Simulated expected price per random dealer roll is about $38.6K (chop about $13.5K). The best of 8 pads averages about $97K chop because of a heavy tail, but the median best-of-8 chop is only about $16K, so 'rebirth in a few heists' takes more like a few dozen. It is still the dominant early-game money source with flat, low risk.
fix: src/server/Systems/DealershipService.luau:777: compute heat from rarity, e.g. `local tier = Rarity.Tiers[(Cars.get(carId) :: any).rarity]; local heat = math.max(PoliceConfig.Heat.dealerSteal, (tier and tier.wantedOnSteal or 0) + 1)`. That gives Legendary 3★ and Mythic/Secret 4★ (WantedService clamps to MAX_STARS). Optionally add a short per-player dealer-theft cooldown in onSteal. Tune chop/sell fractions in src/shared/Config/Economy.luau only if playtests still show it dominating.

summary: Diamond Dragster is a repeatable Robux product worth $15K/s. It can't be stolen or sold and is never lost on rebirth, so stacking it is pay-to-win and breaks the rebirth curve.
evidence: Cars.luau:591-597 `diamond_dragster` has `income = 15000` (more than any Mythic at 4-6K/s), and line 604 has `stealable = false`. MonetizationService.luau:360-382 grants a new one on every purchase with no ownership cap. RebirthService.luau:104-108 keeps every Exclusive car through rebirth. GarageService.luau:860-863 blocks selling it. SPEC §9 promises honest, non-P2W monetization.
failureScenario: A player buys 4 Dragsters, earning $60K/s (×2 with VIP). Rebirth 1 ($750K) takes 6 seconds, R2 takes 25 seconds, and the cars survive every rebirth. Free players can't compete on the leaderboard, and other players have nothing to steal from them.
suggestedFix: Make it a one-per-account pass, or refuse the product when the player already owns one. Lower its income to around Epic or Legendary level (for example $1,500/s) or make it a cosmetic or speed car. Count at most one Exclusive among the cars kept on rebirth.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Cars.luau gives diamond_dragster income 15000 and stealable=false. The MonetizationService.luau:360-382 product handler grants a new car on every purchase with no ownership check. RebirthService._plan (lines 104-108) keeps every Exclusive in addition to the best car, and sellSlot blocks selling Exclusives. Repeat purchases therefore stack permanent, rebirth-proof $15K/s each (more than any Mythic), which contradicts SPEC §9's 'honest, non-P2W' heading. It isn't live yet because the product id is 0. Keep in mind that refusing a paid receipt (returning false gives NotProcessedYet) would just hold or redeliver the purchase forever, so the guard must come before purchase.
fix: Preferred: make the Dragster a one-time GamePass (move it to Monetization.Passes in src/shared/Config/Monetization.luau). In src/server/Systems/MonetizationService.luau, grant one car on PassChanged or refreshPasses when the player has none in the garage or data.exclusives. If it stays a product, have src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau storeItems/refreshStore show 'OWNED' and disable BUY when the snapshot shows a Dragster in the garage or exclusives; the server handler should still grant if a purchase slips through. Either way, consider lowering its income in src/shared/Config/Cars.luau to around Legendary level.

summary: Rebirth silently throws away all uncollected garage cash, and the Rebirth menu doesn't warn about it.
evidence: RebirthService.luau:258-266 calls `Garage.removeSlot(player, slot)` for every slot and ignores the returned record, which carries `uncollected`. Lines 267-268 then reset cash. The menu's 'YOU LOSE' list (MenuController.luau, Rebirth builder around 2760-2765) only mentions cash, cars and slots.
failureScenario: A player who returns after an hour has $500K+ sitting in slot billboards, rebirths straight away, and that money disappears without any notice.
suggestedFix: Before resetting, call `GarageService.collect(player)` (or sum the removed records' `uncollected` and add it to the player's cash before the reset, then show it in the toast). At minimum, add '💰 Uncollected garage cash' to the 'YOU LOSE' list.
verifyReason: Technically true: RebirthService.luau:261 ignores the record removeSlot returns, so its uncollected is dropped. But the suggested fix is wrong. Rebirth sets data.cash = STARTING_CASH right afterwards (line 268), so collecting first, or adding the uncollected sum before the reset, gets wiped as well. Uncollected cash is economically the same as on-hand cash, and the menu already says 'Cash (back to $150)' is lost. The only real harm is a player who doesn't notice the money and so can't spend it on upgrades and tools, which are kept. That makes this a UI clarity issue only.
fix: src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau (Rebirth builder, 'YOU LOSE' list): change the cash line to something like `💵 Cash + uncollected garage cash (back to $150)` and add a hint that upgrades and tools are kept, so the cash should be spent first. Don't add a collect-before-reset in RebirthService, since the cash reset would wipe it.

summary: The Rebirth menu advertises '+10% rare car luck every rebirth', but REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS is never applied anywhere.
evidence: Economy.luau:120 defines `REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS = 0.1`. MenuController.luau:2737 shows it as a rebirth benefit. A grep finds no server use. Street, dealer and traffic rolls use only `EventService.getLuck()` (StreetSpawnService.luau:284, DealershipService.luau:943, TrafficService.luau:785), and spawns are shared across the server, not per player.
failureScenario: Players rebirth partly for the luck boost and get nothing. The Rebirth screen makes a false promise.
suggestedFix: Either remove the luck line from the Rebirth menu, or implement it as a per-player bonus that is actually personal: for example, boost mutation rolls on that player's daily, playtime and referral cars (`Rolls.mutation(1 + rebirths × 0.1)`) or their hot-drop rolls.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Economy.REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS is read only by MenuController (the Rebirth showcase line '🍀 +10% rare car luck ... (every rebirth)'). No server code reads it. Every roll site uses EventService.getLuck() (shared across the server) or a fixed 1 (StreetSpawnService:284, TrafficService:785, DealershipService:943/958, RewardsService.grantCar:358-359, EventService hot drop). The RebirthService header also claims '(and luck)'. The UI makes a false promise.
fix: Simplest: remove the luck text from the Rebirth showcase label in src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau, the '(and luck)' in the src/server/Systems/RebirthService.luau header, and the constant. To keep the promise instead, apply it to personal rolls in src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau grantCar: `Rolls.mutation(1 + (data.rebirths or 0) * Economy.REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS, rng)`, and reword the label to 'better gift mutations'. Shared street, traffic and dealer spawns can't be per-player.

summary: The 'Lose the Cops' product charges Robux even when the player has no wanted level.
evidence: MonetizationService.luau:341-349: the handler treats `callSystem("WantedService","clear",...)` returning ok (pcall success) as a grant. WantedService.luau:351 `if not st or st.stars == 0 then return end` makes no change and raises no error, so the handler returns true and shows 'The cops lost your trail. You're clean!'. The Store card's BUY button (MenuController.luau:1428-1462, promptPurchase 1391-1400) is never disabled based on the Wanted attribute.
failureScenario: A player taps BUY on 'Lose the Cops' while clean, or a cooldown clears the stars just before the receipt is processed. They pay Robux and get nothing, which goes against SPEC §9's honest store.
suggestedFix: In the handler, return false (NotProcessedYet) when `WantedService.getStars(player) == 0`. In the Store, disable or grey out the card with '😇 Not wanted' while the Wanted attribute is 0.
verifyReason: Confirmed. callSystem returns pcall's ok, and WantedService.clear (line 349) returns early with no error when stars == 0. So the clear_wanted handler returns true, records the receipt and says 'You're clean!' with nothing granted. The Store card is never gated on the Wanted attribute. It's latent until the product id is set. The suggested 'return false' fix is harmful: NotProcessedYet makes Roblox redeliver on later joins, where the player is usually clean again, so the purchase is held or looped instead of fixed.
fix: src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau refreshStore: when item.key == 'clear_wanted' and `player:GetAttribute('Wanted')` is not > 0, show '😇 Not wanted' with the button disabled, and refresh on GetAttributeChangedSignal('Wanted'). src/server/Systems/MonetizationService.luau clear_wanted handler: if WantedService.getStars(player) == 0 at receipt time, don't refuse. Grant a stored credit instead (e.g. data.wantedClears += 1) that WantedService consumes automatically the next time stars go above 0, and tell the player so.

summary: Playtime gifts reset every session, so you can rejoin and farm a free Rare, Epic and Legendary car (or about $150K-230K as the full-garage cash fallback) every hour, even while AFK.
evidence: Economy.luau:150-157 gives a Rare at 15 minutes, an Epic at 40 and a Legendary at 60. RewardsService.luau:266 sets `sessionStart = os.clock()` when the state is created, and 931 clears it on leave, so every rejoin starts fresh. There is no AFK or input check. grantCar (356-391) falls back to 50% of the price when the garage is full (Legendary $125K-200K).
failureScenario: Players idle with an anti-AFK tool and rejoin each hour, collecting a Legendary per hour. That outpaces the daily streak (day 7 is only an Epic) and devalues hot drops.
suggestedFix: Store the claimed gift indexes per UTC day in data (one cycle per day), or scale gifts to session length while capping Legendary to once a day. Pause the playtime clock when the player has had no input or character movement for 5+ minutes.
verifyReason: Confirmed in code. sessionStart is set when PState is created and pstates is cleared on leave, so every rejoin restarts the playtime track, and there is no idle check. However, SPEC §RewardsService explicitly says 'Playtime gifts (session-based, not persisted)', and each cycle still needs 60 real minutes in-session, so rejoining yields at most one Rare+Epic+Legendary set per hour played. Roblox's built-in 20-minute idle kick covers plain AFK; only anti-AFK tools get around it. It is a generosity and design concern rather than an exploit of broken code.
fix: If tighter: in src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau, persist playtime progress per UTC day in data (e.g. data.playtime = { day, seconds, claimed }) and accumulate seconds in the existing background loop instead of using os.clock() - sessionStart. Add the field to the DataService template and sanitizer (src/server/Systems/DataService.luau). Optionally stop accumulating while the player's root hasn't moved for 5+ minutes.

summary: Some daily contracts depend on other players ('Steal a car from another player', 'Bonk 3 thieves out of cars') and there is no reroll, so in low-population servers they can't be completed.
evidence: Economy.luau:174 `rob1` (playerSteal) and 177 `bonk3` (defend, goal 3). `_rollContracts` (RewardsService.luau:154-168) picks blindly from the pool with no reroll and nothing aware of server population. `defend` only counts when the victim is driving the attacker's Stolen car (CombatService.luau:869-870). Thefts also need a victim with 3 or more cars and an unlocked garage, plus a 25s cooldown.
failureScenario: A player alone in a server, or with only newbies, gets 'Bonk 3 thieves' and can't make progress all day. One of their three contracts is dead.
suggestedFix: Add a free reroll each day (a remote that swaps one unclaimed contract). Or only roll social contracts when 3 or more other players are online, and lower bonk3 to goal 1.
verifyReason: Confirmed. _rollContracts (RewardsService.luau:154-168) picks 3 distinct-stat contracts deterministically from userId+day, with no reroll and no awareness of who else is online. With 13 distinct stats, about 40% of days include rob1 (playerSteal) or bonk3 (defend, goal 3). CombatService.applyHit counts 'defend' only when the bonked player is driving a Stolen car taken from the attacker, so it needs other players to rob you three times. A newbie with fewer than 3 cars is theft-protected and can never progress it. rob1 needs an online victim with 3 or more cars, an unlocked garage and no victim cooldown. Solo or low-population servers leave these dead all day.
fix: src/shared/Config/Economy.luau: change bonk3 to goal 1 (text 'Bonk a thief out of your car'). Add a once-per-day free reroll: a new client-to-server remote in src/shared/Remotes.luau (e.g. 'RerollContract'), with a handler in src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau that swaps one unclaimed contract for an unused-stat one (persist data.contracts.rerolled = day), and a button in the Contracts tab of src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau.

summary: Selling is a 1-second hold with no confirmation, so a stray hold, especially on mobile, can permanently sell a Mythic or Secret car.
evidence: GarageService.luau:531-546 creates SellPrompt (F, hold 1s, UIOffset 0,84) next to DrivePrompt (E, no hold) on the same chassis. sellSlot (848-881) removes the car immediately. Only Exclusive cars and your last car are protected.
failureScenario: A mobile player taps and holds near their Mythic Galaxy while trying to press Drive and sells a $10M+ car for half its price. There is no undo.
suggestedFix: For Epic and above, add a confirmation step (a server-side 'sell pending' state for 5s that needs a second trigger, or route it through a menu dialog). Alternatively, raise the hold to 2.5s for Legendary and above and show the rarity color on the prompt.
verifyReason: Confirmed. GarageService buildDisplay makes SellPrompt (F / ButtonY, hold 1s, UIOffset 0,84) next to DrivePrompt (E, hold 0) on the same chassis. sellSlot removes the car at once with no confirmation and no rarity scaling; only Exclusive cars and your last car are protected. The 1s hold is a deliberate gesture and the prompts are offset, so accidental sells are uncommon. But the loss is permanent and can be a very valuable car, which makes it a support risk.
fix: src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau buildDisplay: scale the sell hold by rarity (e.g. 1s up to Rare, 2.5s for Epic and above). In sellSlot, for Legendary and above, add a server-side two-step: the first trigger stores ps.sellArm = {slot, until = now + 5} and sends a Notify like 'Hold again to sell your <car> for $X'; only a second trigger inside that window sells.

summary: The 'steal' contract counts when you hotwire, not when you deliver (against pillar 1), and it can be farmed. The stat flag is global to the server, so whether a hot drop counts as a steal is inconsistent.
evidence: progress('steal') fires at hotwire time in StreetSpawnService.luau:255, TrafficService.luau:754, VehicleService.luau:1199 and DealershipService.luau:778. `canHotwireLoot` (VehicleService.luau:1170-1181) does not exclude the car's own claimer. `HideForUserId` (line 1272) only hides the prompt on the client, so an exploiter can re-hotwire their own abandoned loot for +1 steal each time. RewardsService.luau:256/464 sets `explicitStats` server-wide, and the fallback at line 787 only works until any explicit call. Hot drop claims (EventService.luau:760-763) never report 'steal', so they count only if they happen before the first explicit steal on the server.
failureScenario: 'Steal 12 cars' can be done by carjacking traffic and jumping out 12 times without ever driving home. Whether a hot drop counts toward it depends on server history.
suggestedFix: Report 'steal' on successful delivery in GarageService.onDelivery (Loot) and TheftService.complete, and remove it from the hotwire paths. Make `explicitStats` per player, or delete the fallback for 'steal' and 'playerSteal' now that every source reports explicitly. In canHotwireLoot, reject `player.UserId == car.ownerUserId`.
verifyReason: Confirmed but minor. progress('steal') fires on hotwire, carjack and dealer theft (StreetSpawnService:255, TrafficService:754, VehicleService:1199, DealershipService:778, TheftService:1199), not on delivery. canHotwireLoot doesn't reject the claimer, and HideForUserId is only a client-side hide, so an exploiter can re-hotwire their own Common loot (0★) for +1 each time. The server still enforces the hold time. A legit player can also carjack traffic repeatedly. explicitStats in RewardsService is server-wide, so the statWatch fallback for 'steal' (which counts deliveries, hot drops included) only works until the first explicit hotwire on the server, usually within seconds. That makes hot-drop counting inconsistent, but the effect is tiny.
fix: src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau: remove 'steal' and 'playerSteal' from DERIVED_COUNTERS, since every source now reports explicitly. That removes the server-history dependence. src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau canHotwireLoot: return false when `car.ownerUserId == player.UserId` (the claimer re-enters through EnterPrompt, which adds no heat and no progress). Moving 'steal' to delivery is an optional design change in GarageService.onDelivery and TheftService.complete.

summary: When the garage is full, the messages never mention unlocking a slot. The only way to unlock is a prompt on a pad inside the garage, and there is no menu entry for it.
evidence: GarageService.luau:1106 says 'Garage full! Sell a car or chop it at the Chop Shop'. DealershipService.luau:680 says 'Your garage is full! Sell a car first.' Unlocking only exists as GarageClient's local UnlockPrompt (GarageClient.luau:455-456). Slot 5 costs just $1,500 (Economy.luau:18).
failureScenario: A new player delivers a 5th car, is told to sell or chop it, and sells a car instead of spending $1.5K on a slot they never knew existed.
suggestedFix: Add 'or unlock slot N for $X (glowing pad in your garage)' to the full-garage messages, with a waypoint to the next pad. Also list slot unlocks in the Gear Shop.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Every garage-full message (GarageService:1106, DealershipService:678/785, TheftService:349/701/1252, RewardsService:389) only suggests selling or chopping. Slot unlocking only exists as a client-side UnlockPrompt on the next pad (GarageClient renderPad/ensureUnlockPrompt). That pad does pulse green with 'UNLOCK $1,500' inside the garage, which softens the problem, but nothing points players to it from elsewhere.
fix: Add a shared helper (e.g. GarageService.fullHint(player)) that returns ' or unlock slot N for $X at the glowing pad in your garage' when slotsUnlocked < Economy.MAX_SLOTS, and append it to the full-garage messages in src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau, src/server/Systems/DealershipService.luau and src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau.

summary: VIP offline earnings can be paid at the non-VIP rate because they are calculated 3s after load, while the pass lookup is still retrying.
evidence: RewardsService.luau:695-701 waits OFFLINE_DELAY (3s), then calls `hasPass(player, "vip")` once. MonetizationService.luau:534 runs refreshPasses in parallel, and each UserOwnsGamePassAsync failure waits `task.wait(attempt)` (line 514, so 1+2s). Until the lookup succeeds, `owned` is empty.
failureScenario: On a slow join, a VIP gets 0.3× instead of the promised doubled offline earnings.
suggestedFix: In grantOffline, wait until MonetizationService reports the pass lookup finished (expose `passesReady(player)` or a signal, with a timeout), or top up the difference when PassChanged('vip') fires within the first 30s.
verifyReason: Confirmed but rare. grantOffline waits OFFLINE_DELAY (3s) after data load, then reads hasPass('vip') once. refreshPasses runs in parallel from PlayerAdded. vip is first in PassOrder, so a normal lookup finishes well within that window. Only when UserOwnsGamePassAsync fails and retries (task.wait(1), then 2) could a VIP be paid OFFLINE_RATE instead of VIP_OFFLINE_RATE. It's also moot until the vip id is non-zero.
fix: src/server/Systems/MonetizationService.luau: set a per-player passesReady flag (or Signal) at the end of refreshPasses and expose MonetizationService.passesReady(player). src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau grantOffline: after OFFLINE_DELAY, wait until passesReady(player) or about 10s have passed, then compute the amount.

summary: The VIP pass promises a 'VIP tag', but only the buyer sees a crown on their own HUD. Nothing is visible to other players.
evidence: Monetization.luau:15 description reads '2x cash forever, VIP tag, double offline earnings.' MonetizationService.luau:161-169 only sets the player attribute VIP. The only reader is HUDController.luau:1067 (local crown). There is no overhead tag, chat tag or garage sign marker.
failureScenario: Buyers get no social status from VIP, and other players never see VIP, which weakens pass sales.
suggestedFix: Add a 👑 to the overhead name or garage sign (PlotService sign Stats line) and a TextChatService chat tag for players with VIP=true.
verifyReason: Confirmed. The VIP description promises a 'VIP tag', but MonetizationService only sets the VIP player attribute, and its only reader is HUDController:1067 (a crown on the local HUD). Nothing in PlotService signs, overhead names, the leaderboard or TextChatService shows VIP to other players.
fix: Either drop 'VIP tag' from the description in src/shared/Config/Monetization.luau, or add a visible tag: a 👑 prefix on the owner's garage sign in src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau when player:GetAttribute('VIP'), and/or a client TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage handler that sets a gold [VIP] PrefixText for senders whose VIP attribute is true.

summary: Daily streak rewards and codes pay fixed cash ($500-$15K), so they are worthless after the first hour and give little reason to come back.
evidence: Economy.luau:139-147: day 1-3 and 5 pay fixed cash of 500, 1500, 4000 and 15000. Codes at 196-201 pay 1000-5000 fixed. A mid-game player earns $10K+/s.
failureScenario: By day 2, claiming the daily reward feels pointless. The streak pillar adds nothing compared with playtime gifts or a single heist.
suggestedFix: Convert the cash days to incomeMinutes (for example 2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 minutes) with the current amounts as minimums. Make day 7 a choice of a mutated Epic or a Legendary.
verifyReason: Confirmed but a tuning matter. DAILY_REWARDS days 1, 2, 3 and 5 and every Code pay fixed cash ($500-$15K), while days 4 and 6 already scale with income (incomeMinutes). For mid-game players earning thousands per second, the fixed days become trivial.
fix: src/shared/Config/Economy.luau: change the cash days to incomeMinutes (e.g. 2, 5, 10, 20) and keep day 7's car. RewardsService._incomeMinutesReward already floors at $500. If larger floors are wanted, add an optional `min` field and honor it in src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau grant().

summary: Buying Lockdown while one is already active doesn't add time (it uses max, not stack), so the second purchase is mostly wasted.
evidence: PlotService.luau:1303 `st.lockedUntil = math.max(st.lockedUntil, now + math.min(seconds, 3600))`, called by the lock_10 handler (MonetizationService.luau:327-339) with 600s.
failureScenario: A player with 8 minutes of lockdown left buys another and ends up with 10 minutes, not 18.
suggestedFix: For the product path, stack the time: `max(lockedUntil, now) + seconds`, capped at 1h. Or grey out the Store card while a lockdown is active.
verifyReason: Confirmed. PlotService.lockFor (line 1303) uses math.max(lockedUntil, now + seconds), so buying Lockdown with 8 minutes left ends at 10 minutes, not 18. The same applies if a regular button lock is active. The only other caller, tryLock, refuses when the garage is already locked, so switching to stacking only changes the product path.
fix: src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau lockFor: `st.lockedUntil = math.min(math.max(st.lockedUntil, now) + seconds, now + 3600)`. That's safe because tryLock never calls it while locked.

summary: Carjacking a car in traffic always adds 1★, whatever its rarity, so carjacking a Mythic is much safer than hotwiring a parked one.
evidence: TrafficService.luau:753 `addStealHeat(player, PoliceConfig.Heat.carjack, "carjack")` with Police.luau:26 `carjack = 1`, while street steals use `tier.wantedOnSteal` (Rarity Mythic is 3).
failureScenario: A Mythic in traffic is a low-risk steal, which undercuts the 'rarer means hotter chase' design.
suggestedFix: Use `max(Heat.carjack, tier.wantedOnSteal)` for carjacks.
verifyReason: Confirmed but matches SPEC. TrafficService.onCarjack (line 753) uses the flat Heat.carjack (1), as SPEC §Traffic states, so a carjacked Mythic gives 1★ against 3★ for a parked one. Traffic uses street weights (Mythic 0.08%), so this rarely comes up. It is a design inconsistency with the 'stars rise with rarity' pillar, not a bug.
fix: src/server/Systems/TrafficService.luau onCarjack: `local tier = Rarity.Tiers[(Cars.get(car.carId) :: any).rarity]; local heat = VehicleService.addStealHeat(player, math.max(PoliceConfig.Heat.carjack, tier and tier.wantedOnSteal or 0), 'carjack')`.

summary: Collecting only fires on a fresh Touched by the character. Standing on the pad or driving over it collects nothing.
evidence: GarageService.luau:817-844 only resolves a player from a character part. A car chassis resolves to Workspace.Vehicles and is ignored. There is no loop that collects while the player stands on the pad.
failureScenario: Players who park on the pad, or wait on it for income, see the glow but nothing happens until they step off and back on.
suggestedFix: While the owner's root is inside the pad's box, collect every 1s (a poll in watchOutCars or the tick), and also accept a touch from the owner's driven car's chassis.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Collecting is wired only to CollectPad.Touched (GarageService ~1313), with onCollectTouched resolving only character parts. A player standing still on the pad gets nothing new until a fresh touch, and a driven car's chassis is ignored. This is the common Roblox collect-pad pattern and walking around retriggers it, so the impact is small.
fix: src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau: in the existing 1s income tick, for each player whose plot has uncollected > 0, check whether their HumanoidRootPart is over the CollectPad (pad.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(pos) inside half the size in X/Z, with a few studs of Y margin) and call GarageService.collect(player) when COLLECT_DEBOUNCE has passed. Optionally also accept a hit whose ancestor is the owner's currently driven car.

summary: The bump-stop balls ride 0.45 studs above the road, lower than the 0.6 curb. Every curb mount without a ramp hits a solid sphere: the car loses speed and gets thrown upward.
evidence: CarBuilder.luau:159-160 BUMPSTOP_SIZE=1, BUMPSTOP_CLEARANCE=0.25. CarBuilder.luau:547-565 adds collidable Balls at x=0, z=axle, bottom 0.25. VehicleController.luau:34 RIDE_LIFT=0.2, so at rest the ball bottom is at 0.45; at 100 studs/s downforce adds about 0.07 compression (0.38), and with hypercar nitro it drops to about 0.07. Map.luau:18 CURB_HEIGHT=0.6. The suspension rays ignore near-vertical faces (VehicleController.luau:46, 613) and only climb once the hub is over the curb. The ball is at the same Z as the axle and sticks out 0.36 studs ahead at curb height, so it hits the curb edge first. The test at tests/spec/vehicle.spec.luau:332-334 only checks the chassis bottom, not the bump stops.
failureScenario: A player cuts a corner or swerves onto a sidewalk anywhere except a DrivewayRamp at 60 studs/s. The ball strikes the curb edge at about 45°. With elasticity 0 the impulse removes the velocity into the edge: roughly 30 studs/s of forward speed is lost and about 30 studs/s of upward speed is added, plus a pitch kick. The client crash detector shakes the camera. Above about 110 studs/s the server also applies crash damage (Δv > 55). This happens constantly in a city full of curbs and goes against pillar 2.
suggestedFix: Either raise BUMPSTOP_CLEARANCE so that clearance + RIDE_LIFT is more than CURB_HEIGHT + 0.2 (for example 0.65), or have VehicleController set the BumpStop parts to CanCollide=false locally while it runs and restore them in destroy() (the server does the same for police). Extend the vehicle spec test to assert that bump-stop bottom + RIDE_LIFT is greater than CURB_HEIGHT.
verifyReason: Confirmed. CarBuilder.luau:159-160,547-565 places two collidable massless Balls (d=1, bottom 0.25) at x=0, z=axleF/axleR. Nothing in the repo turns them off: no CollisionGroups exist, and grep finds no BumpStop handling in PoliceService, VehicleService or VehicleController. The tracer's claim that 'the server does the same for police' is wrong, so police cars snag too. At rest the ball bottom is 0.25+RIDE_LIFT 0.2 = 0.45, below CURB_HEIGHT 0.6. Sidewalk strips are vertical-faced blocks (MapBuilder 1116-1210); only DrivewayRamp curb cuts are wedges. Suspension rays go straight down from the hub (VehicleController 613), so they only reach the curb top once the hub is over it. At curb height the ball reaches about 0.357 ahead of the axle, so it strikes the curb's top corner with a roughly 44° normal. Elasticity is 0. Downforce adds 0.002·v²/(4·68) of compression: about 0.07 at 100 studs/s, and about 0.38 at 227 (hypercar nitro), which leaves about 0.07 of clearance. These numbers match the tracer. With pitch inertia included, my estimate is about 22 studs/s of forward speed lost and 22 gained upward at 60 studs/s, a bit less than the claimed 30, but still a hard snag. Server crash damage (Δv>55) starts around 110 studs/s. The rear ball hits the curb again after the front wheels climb. The test at vehicle.spec 332-334 checks only the chassis bottom.
fix: Do not just raise BUMPSTOP_CLEARANCE. At 0.65 the ball still dips under 0.6 at speed (0.85-0.38), and cars resting without a controller sink 0.65 into the road. Instead, change src/shared/Vehicle/VehicleController.luau: in new(), for every model child named "BumpStop" that is a BasePart, store its CanCollide and set it false; restore it in destroy() (pcall, skip if the part is gone). On the driver's client this changes only the owner's local simulation, which is the one that counts for a client-owned assembly. On the server (police, and the F4 settle controller) it replicates harmlessly. While driving, the chassis box (bottom ≥0.95 with the lift) still keeps the car off the ground. In tests/spec/vehicle.spec.luau, add a check that BumpStops are CanCollide=false after VC.new and true again after destroy, and a note/assert that stop bottom + RIDE_LIFT < CURB_HEIGHT, which is why they must be disabled.

summary: The zone pass acts on a client-reported car position before the watchdog checks it. A cheater can teleport their client-owned car into their own drop-off, the Chop Shop or a Spray booth and get an instant delivery, chop or wanted wipe.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:146-147 ZONE_TICK=0.2, WATCHDOG_TICK=0.5. In the Heartbeat at VehicleService.luau:1739-1746 the zone pass runs before the watchdog. zonePass (VehicleService.luau:1460-1498) reads car.chassis.CFrame.Position and calls fireDelivery or ChopAttempt:Fire or SprayAttempt:Fire straight away, with no plausibility check against st.wdCFrame. GarageService.onDelivery (GarageService.luau:1021+) and TheftService.complete (TheftService.luau:1223+) do no distance or time checks either. The car is destroyed on delivery, so a later watchdog rewind does nothing.
failureScenario: An exploiter hotwires a Mythic Hot Drop or dealership car (or steals from another player's garage). The client owns the car, so the exploiter sets its CFrame inside their own Dropoff box. Within 0.2 s the DeliveryAttempt fires, the car is stored, or for a Stolen car TheftService.complete transfers the victim's car. The watchdog never runs on it. The same trick into a spray booth clears 5★ instantly. This skips the core 'every steal is a getaway' loop and the fair-theft pillar.
suggestedFix: In zonePass, run _watchdogVerdict for that car (displacement since st.wdCFrame vs cap*(now-wdAt)+slack) before acting on any zone, and skip the zone if it fails. Also require the car to be inside the drop-off on two consecutive zone ticks, or require a passed watchdog sample taken inside the zone. Alternatively, record a server breadcrumb (last validated position and time) and reject zone entries whose implied speed is above the cap.
verifyReason: Confirmed. The Heartbeat at VehicleService 1739-1746 runs zonePass (every 0.2 s) before watchdogPass (every 0.5 s). zonePass (1460-1498) reads the live, client-replicated car.chassis.CFrame.Position and immediately calls fireDelivery, ChopAttempt or SprayAttempt. It does not compare against st.wdCFrame and does not check wdRevokedUntil. The handlers trust it fully. GarageService.onDelivery (1021+) checks no distance or time and destroys the car straight away for Loot/Owned. TheftService.complete (1223+) only checks thief/victim state. WantedService.onSprayAttempt (541+) only charges cash and clears the stars. Once the car is destroyed, the watchdog never samples the teleport, so a CFrame write from the owning client becomes an instant delivery, chop or wanted wipe.
fix: In src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau zonePass, before any zone action: skip the car if now < st.wdRevokedUntil. Then compute disp = flat(pos - st.wdCFrame.Position).Magnitude, dt = min(now - st.wdAt, WATCHDOG_MAX_DT) and hSpeed, and call VehicleService._watchdogVerdict(hSpeed, disp, dt, getSpeedCap(car)). If it returns a verdict, call violate(car, player, st, verdict, ...) and continue without firing any zone signal. Also move runPass('watchdog') above runPass('zone') in the Heartbeat. For extra safety, fire a zone only when the last watchdog-accepted position (st.wdCFrame.Position) is also inside it, which costs at most 0.5 s of delay. Add a vehicleservice.spec test: a car teleported into its drop-off does not fire DeliveryAttempt. Note that the remaining per-tick hop allowance is F5's problem.

summary: Locking the garage during a theft teleports the thief and the victim's stolen car outside the laser gate. The defence helps the attacker escape.
evidence: PlotService.luau:1229-1267: pushOut checks whether the intruder is seated in a 'Vehicle'-tagged car and, if so, calls carModel:PivotTo onto the driveway outside (FRONT_Z-12). It does not eject the driver. PlotService.lockFor (PlotService.luau:1297-1310) calls pushOut immediately and then every PUSH_INTERVAL=0.5 s (PlotService.luau:40). TheftService only checks the lock when the theft starts (TheftService.luau:336-337), so a victim can lock mid-theft.
failureScenario: A thief is driving the victim's Legendary out of a back slot. The victim runs to the LOCK pad. The lock instantly places the thief, still in the stolen car, on the driveway past the gate, skipping the interior and any bonk/zap counterplay. The victim's 'timed laser lock' defence gives the thief a free exit (pillar 5).
suggestedFix: In pushOut, when the car is Stolen from this plot's owner or the intruder is not the car's owner/claimer, call VehicleService.eject(car) and push only the character. TheftService's drop rules then leave the car inside and the victim gets the Recover prompt. Never move other people's vehicles.
verifyReason: Confirmed. PlotService.pushOut (1229-1267) checks whether the intruder sits in a 'Vehicle'-tagged model and, if so, PivotTo's the whole car with the driver still seated onto the driveway at FRONT_Z-12-2. lockFor (1297-1310) calls pushOut immediately, and the heartbeat repeats it every PUSH_INTERVAL 0.5 s (1602-1619). TheftService checks the lock only in the start gate (336-337, 1034). This contradicts SPEC §6 line 106, which says only the character is pivoted out. While locked, the gate is CanCollide=true (applyLockVisual), so without this push a mid-theft lock would trap the thief inside. Instead the lock teleports the thief and the stolen car past the gate, and the victim's lock helps the attacker.
fix: In src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau pushOut, resolve the car with sys('VehicleService').fromModel(carModel). If car.kind == 'Stolen' (car.data.theft from this plot's owner), call VehicleService.eject(car) first. TheftService's DriverChanged→markDropped then leaves the car inside and gives the victim the Recover prompt. After the eject, pivot only the character to the driveway, as the else branch already does. For any other vehicle (the intruder's own Owned or Loot car), move it with VehicleService.teleport(car, cf), which pivots and calls resetWatchdog (this also fixes F7), instead of a raw carModel:PivotTo.

summary: No server-side settling controller runs after exit, although the spec requires one. Every exited, dropped or released car falls about 0.45 studs onto its two centreline bump stops, rolls onto the chassis edge, and is anchored there.
evidence: SPEC.md:115 says the server simulates the car settling after exit, and SPEC.md:261 says controllers are kept for cars settling after exit. In VehicleService.luau:841-853, setDriver(nil) only disables the seat and calls SetNetworkOwner(nil); no VehicleController is created anywhere in VehicleService (grep shows only PoliceService/VehicleClient/WheelAnimator use it). The client destroys its controller at VehicleClient.luau:984-986. The two bump stops are on the centreline (CarBuilder.luau:547-553). The CarBuilder integration doc admits a car can 'tip about 11° sideways'. lifePass then anchors the tilted car (VehicleService.luau:1634-1645). TrafficService.release (TrafficService.luau:686-712) removes the AlignPosition from rammed traffic cars with no replacement.
failureScenario: A player exits any car, or a thief is bonked out, or traffic gets rammed. The car drops and leans 11.5° (sedan: atan(0.65/3.2)); a monster truck (chassis bottom 2.7) leans about 33° with its non-colliding wheels sinking into the road. If the player was moving, the car slides on two low-friction balls with no brake. After 10 s it is anchored at that angle, so parked and abandoned cars across the city look broken.
suggestedFix: Two options. (a) In setDriver(nil), create a server VehicleController(isServer=true) with zero input. Step it from a server PreSimulation loop until it is anchored, then destroy it, and also destroy it in seat(). The client's _suppressForeignMovers already handles replicated movers. (b) Replace the two centreline balls with four collidable balls at the wheel hubs (radius ≈ WheelRadius-0.1) that VehicleController turns non-collidable while it runs (this also fixes F1). Also pivot the car to a level rest pose before anchoring.
verifyReason: Confirmed. SPEC.md:115 and :261 call for a server settling controller, and the integration doc expects VehicleService to destroy it on sit. No such controller exists: VehicleController is created only by PoliceService (921) and the client. setDriver(nil) (841-853) only disables the seat and calls SetNetworkOwner(nil). Client-created movers never replicate, so once the server owns the car nothing holds it up, and it falls onto the two centreline balls. That support is unstable on a line, and the chassis COM is on the centreline because the other parts are Massless. CarBuilder's own doc admits a tilt of about 11°. The bigfoot chassis bottom is 2.7 (CarBuilder 1448), so its tilt is much larger. lifePass (1634-1645) then anchors the car in whatever pose it has. TrafficService.release (686-712) cleans up the Align movers with no replacement. One sub-claim is overstated: 'slides with no brake'. Ball friction 0.3, averaged with the road's, still stops the car quickly.
fix: Two fixes in src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau. (1) When a car loses its driver (the setDriver(nil) path), and also through a public VehicleService.settle(car) that TrafficService.release calls for rammed/knocked cars, create VehicleController.new(model, def, {isServer=true}) with zero input. Step it from one server RunService.PreSimulation loop over the settling set. Destroy it when lifePass anchors the car, when seat() or setDriver(player) gives the car a driver (before SetNetworkOwner(player)), and in destroy(). The client's _suppressForeignMovers already covers the replicated movers. (2) Before setting chassis.Anchored=true in lifePass, if the car is tilted (UpVector.Y < 0.98), PivotTo a level pose at RideHeight above a server ground raycast. Do not add hub balls (the tracer's option b): bull_charger and family_suv are already at the 40-part cap.

summary: The watchdog is too lenient. The cap is 2.1× top speed with no nitro check, vertical movement is ignored, and holding still accrues up to 3 s of teleport allowance. Speed hacks, car flying and 800-stud hops all pass.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:386-392: cap = topSpeed×1.35×1.3×1.2, applied to every car, nitro or not. VehicleService.luau:1561-1562 uses flat() displacement and velocity only, so Y is never checked. VehicleService.luau:1564 sets dt = min(now-wdAt, 3), and VehicleService.luau:1576-1580 does not advance wdAt while disp ≤ 0.01, so the allowance grows to cap·3+10. Single samples under 1.5·cap need two strikes (VehicleService.luau:1566-1570). PoliceService bustPass requires |ΔY| < 10 (PoliceService.luau:1781).
failureScenario: An exploiter in a 130-top-speed car drives at a steady 270 studs/s without a violation. They can also park for 2.9 s and then jump about 800 studs in one tick. Or they fly the car 15+ studs up, out of bust range and over traffic and cops, and are never flagged. Getaways become trivial.
suggestedFix: Use topSpeed×SPEED_CAP_MULT×GRACE as the base and only multiply by NITRO_SPEED_MULT for short windows (a full tank lasts at most nitroSeconds of the owner's upgrade, so the server can bound it). Advance wdAt every tick and cap the stall allowance (for example 1 s). Add a vertical check: sustained height above ground (server raycast) over N seconds, or upward speed above the ramp-launch maximum without a recent ramp contact, counts as a violation. Combine with F2.
verifyReason: Confirmed. _speedCap (386-392) is topSpeed×1.35×1.3×1.2 ≈ 2.1×topSpeed for every car. The spec test even locks this in, so a sustained 1.6× over the real nitro maximum passes; for a 130-top-speed car the cap is about 274. watchdogPass measures flat() displacement and horizontal speed only, so Y is never checked, while police bustPass requires |ΔY| < 10 (1781). The allowance accrues because wdAt only advances when disp > 0.01 or after 3 s (1576-1580), and dt = min(now-wdAt, 3). A car held still for about 2.9 s can therefore jump cap·2.9+10 in one tick: about 437 studs for a Rustbucket and about 1070 for a 175 car. The test 'lag stall: allowance accrues with dt' shows this was intended, but it can be exploited. Speed violations under 1.5×cap need two strikes. Part of the nitro choice is deliberate (every car has a nitro tank), but the vertical gap and the stall allowance are real holes.
fix: In src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau and src/shared/Config/Vehicle.luau: (a) cut WATCHDOG_MAX_DT to about 1 s and update the 'lag stall' expectation in tests/spec/vehicleservice.spec.luau. (b) Add a vertical check on each watchdog tick: raycast down from the chassis (exclude Vehicles and characters); if there is no ground within about 40 studs for longer than about 4 s in a row (more than the MegaRamp's airtime), or upward displacement per tick exceeds a ramp-launch bound, call violate(). (c) Optionally take NITRO_SPEED_MULT out of the base cap and allow the nitro band only while a server-side budget lasts (the player's nitro-upgrade seconds plus NITRO_REFILL_PER_SEC, unlimited with the Infinite Nitro pass). Update the cap test to match. Do this together with F2.

summary: A voluntary exit (F/E/A/EXIT) never moves the character out of the car. The avatar is left standing on top of the invisible collision box inside the visible body.
evidence: VehicleClient.exit (VehicleClient.luau:1178-1186) only re-enables Jumping and sets Humanoid.Jump. On the server, onOccupantChanged with humanoid==nil (VehicleService.luau:864-869) calls setDriver(nil) without nudgeOut. Only kickOccupant (VehicleService.luau:777-790), used for server ejects, nudges. The seat top is at roofBot-3.45, between 0.45 and beltY-0.2 (CarBuilder.luau:752-754), which is inside the 0.9-2.7 chassis box (CarBuilder.luau:641/449).
failureScenario: A player presses F to hop out next to a car they want to hotwire. Their character pops up onto the chassis top (about 2.7 studs), so the head clips through the roof and the torso sits inside the cabin. They have to walk off the car body before doing anything. It looks glitchy every time and makes quick car swaps awkward.
suggestedFix: In onOccupantChanged, when the occupant becomes nil and car.driver ~= nil, call nudgeOut(car, car.driver.Character) before setDriver(nil). It is already raycast-safe and picks the driver's side first. Alternatively, have the client ask the server to exit through a remote that runs VehicleService.eject.
verifyReason: Confirmed. VehicleClient.exit (1178-1186) only re-enables Jumping and sets Humanoid.Jump. On the server, onOccupantChanged with a nil occupant (864-869) only calls setDriver(nil); nudgeOut runs only through kickOccupant(car, true), i.e. eject or unauthorized occupants. Nothing on the client repositions the character (CombatClient handles knockback only). The seat top is clamped between 0.45 and beltY-0.2 (CarBuilder 752), inside the collidable chassis box (for example 0.9-2.7), and every visible body part is non-collidable. After the jump the character resolves onto the chassis top, inside the visible cabin with its head through the roof.
fix: In src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau onOccupantChanged, in the humanoid == nil branch: if car.driver is set, take char = car.driver.Character. If that character's Humanoid has no SeatPart (it has not just sat in another seat), call nudgeOut(car, char) before setDriver(car, nil). nudgeOut is a local defined above (line 725) and is already raycast-safe.

summary: PlotService pushOut moves a driven car with a server PivotTo but never resets the watchdog. For slow cars in the back slots, the watchdog flags a 'teleport' and rubber-bands the car back inside the locked garage, freezing it for 2 s.
evidence: PlotService.luau:1244-1251 calls carModel:PivotTo with no VehicleService.teleport or resetWatchdog call; both exist at VehicleService.luau:990-1009 and nothing calls them. The push target is (0/±7, FRONT_Z-12-2 = -58) (PlotService.luau:250-255, 1246). From slot z=38 at x=±33 (Map.luau:68-69) the flat distance is about 100 studs. The watchdog allowance is cap·0.5+10 (VehicleService.luau:399, 1564); for a Rustbucket (topSpeed 70) that is 147·0.5+10 = 84 < 100, so the verdict is 'teleport' and violate() pivots back to wdCFrame, inside the garage (VehicleService.luau:1524-1530).
failureScenario: A Common or Uncommon car (topSpeed ≤ ~86) is being driven by a non-owner from a back slot when the lock engages. It is teleported out, snapped back in, frozen with server ownership for 2 s, then pushed out again on the next 0.5 s tick, with a warn spam in the logs. If F3 is fixed by ejecting instead, this goes away; otherwise any server move of a driven car needs a watchdog reset.
suggestedFix: Route every server-side move of a driven car through VehicleService.teleport(car, cf), which pivots and resets the watchdog. Use it in PlotService.pushOut (or apply the F3 fix and stop moving cars there). Add a lint or grep rule: no model:PivotTo on Workspace.Vehicles models outside VehicleService.
verifyReason: Confirmed but narrow. pushOut uses a raw carModel:PivotTo, and nothing calls VehicleService.teleport or resetWatchdog. From back slots (±33, 38) to the push spot (0/±7, -58) is about 100 studs. With dt≈0.5 the allowance is cap·0.5+10, which is below 100 when topSpeed is under about 85, so slow cars get a 'teleport' verdict. violate() then rewinds them to wdCFrame inside the garage and holds server ownership for 2 s; the next pushOut moves them out again. At the end of the revoke, wdCFrame is reset to the current pose, so it is a single rubber-band with one warn, not spam. It only happens when a lock lands during a theft of a slow car from a back slot, and the F3 fix removes it.
fix: This is covered by the F3 fix in src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau: eject from Stolen cars, and move any other car with VehicleService.teleport(car, cf), which calls resetWatchdog. As a general rule, server code outside VehicleService must never PivotTo a driven Workspace.Vehicles model directly.

summary: DriveCar always spawns at the fixed DRIVE_OUT_SPAWN with no clearance check. Taking out a second car while the first sits unoccupied in the aisle spawns them overlapping, and the physics engine flings them apart.
evidence: GarageService.luau:883-950: driveSlot only checks that the player is not driving, then spawns at plotToWorld(index, DRIVE_OUT_SPAWN) (GarageService.luau:916-922) and seats immediately. Map.luau:76 DRIVE_OUT_SPAWN=(0,0,8). An exited Owned car stays where it was for OWNED_RETURN_AFTER=20 s (Config/Vehicle.luau:72; VehicleService.luau:1648-1651).
failureScenario: A player takes out the Rustbucket, changes their mind, presses F, walks to slot 3 and presses Drive. The new car spawns inside the old one. Depenetration launches one or both cars (possibly through the roof), the watchdog sees a fling and revokes control, and both may take crash damage once the 1 s grace ends. A very common 'pick a different car' flow ends in chaos.
suggestedFix: Before spawning, query the DRIVE_OUT_SPAWN box with GetPartBoundsInBox and an OverlapParams filter on Workspace.Vehicles. If the player's own unoccupied Owned car is there, send it home first (returnHome or destroy plus restoreSlot), or pick the next free aisle offset. Refuse with a toast if the spot is blocked by something else.
verifyReason: Confirmed. driveSlot (GarageService 883-950) checks only that the player is not driving and is near or in the plot, then spawns at plotToWorld(index, DRIVE_OUT_SPAWN) with no overlap check and seats the player. There is no one-car-out rule (ps.outCars is per slot). An exited Owned car stays put until OWNED_RETURN_AFTER=20 s (VehicleService 1648-1651), and it never counts as delivered while leftGarage is false. So 'Drive A, press F, Drive B' spawns B inside A, both unanchored, and depenetration flings them.
fix: In src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau driveSlot, before setting ps.states[slot]/removeDisplay: for each car in ps.outCars with no driver that is not destroyed, park it home, reusing onDelivery's Owned branch (car.data.delivered=true; destroyCar(car,'parked'); ps.outCars[s]=nil; GarageService.restoreSlot(player, s)). Then run Workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox over the spawn footprint (about Length×Width×6 at the DRIVE_OUT_SPAWN world CFrame) with OverlapParams Include {VehicleService.getFolder()}. If anything is still there, notify 'Clear the exit first!' and return false.

summary: The 'sunk car' check sits at y < -30, but the seabed is at -14, so it never fires. Cars driven into the ocean keep driving on the seabed, and cops (rubber-banded below -8 or past x/z 900) can never follow, so the sea is a bust-proof hideout.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:141 LOST_Y = WATER_LEVEL-28 = -30. MapBuilder.luau:65 SEABED_Y = WATER_LEVEL-12 = -14. VehicleService.luau:1609-1617 cleans up only below LOST_Y. VehicleController raycasts use IgnoreWater=true (VehicleController.luau:336), so suspension and drive keep working underwater. PoliceService.luau:1845-1854 rubber-bands units below WATER_LEVEL-6 or past SAND_EXTENT, and bustPass needs |ΔY| < 10 (PoliceService.luau:1781).
failureScenario: A 5★ suspect drives off the beach or the open end of the pier and parks on the seabed past x=900. Police units that follow are teleported away, a bust is impossible, and the car is never 'lost', so Owned or Stolen cars are never sent home. The player sits there until the stars decay (or keeps them indefinitely while the line-of-sight raycast, which also ignores water, keeps 'seeing' them).
suggestedFix: Set LOST_Y just below WATER_LEVEL, or better, treat a chassis below WATER_LEVEL-2 for more than about 2 s as sunk. Eject the driver, return Owned and Stolen cars home, and destroy Loot. Optionally make VehicleController zero drive force when the chassis is underwater (Terrain:ReadVoxels or a water-level check).
verifyReason: Confirmed with one correction. VehicleService.LOST_Y = WATER_LEVEL-28 = -30, but the water bottom is -12 and the slope/seabed reaches -14 (MapBuilder 65, 2547). Water runs from about 880 out to the boundary wall at 960, so a sunk car never trips lifePass. Controller rays use IgnoreWater and keep driving on the seabed. Police units below -8 or past |x|/|z| 900 get rubber-banded (PoliceService 1845-1854), and a bust needs ≤16 studs (BUST_RADIUS). A suspect parked at x≈930-956 underwater therefore cannot be busted. Correction: Stolen cars ARE handled, by TheftService.LOST_Y = WATER_LEVEL-6 (1544). The gap is Loot and Owned cars and the bust immunity.
fix: In src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau, set VehicleService.LOST_Y = MapConfig.WATER_LEVEL - 6, the same value as TheftService.LOST_Y and PoliceService's lost threshold; only the underwater seabed is below -8. lifePass then ejects the driver, sends Owned cars home and destroys Loot, and TheftService keeps handling Stolen. Optionally make it a 1-2 s debounce.

summary: Anchored kinds (Parked, Dealership, HotDrop) are spawned 0.3 studs above the ground and never drop. WheelAnimator's anchored 'settled' early-out stops the wheel bob from ever correcting a car first seen from more than 140 studs away, so street cars hover 0.3 studs above the road.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:623-624 pivots to ground*(RideHeight+0.3) for every kind, and VehicleService.luau:675-676 anchors Parked/Dealership/HotDrop at that height. WheelAnimator.luau:307-312 returns early for anchored cars once rig.settled. WheelAnimator.luau:339: doBob only if dist ≤ 140; otherwise the target is 0, and WheelAnimator.luau:366 marks the car settled. rebuildNear never clears settled when the distance shrinks.
failureScenario: Parked street cars spawn at least 60 studs from players and are usually first seen from far away. When the player walks up to hotwire one, the tyres float 0.3 studs off the asphalt with a visible gap, which reads as cheap.
suggestedFix: In spawn, use +0.3 only for unanchored kinds (anchored ones should sit at exactly RideHeight). In WheelAnimator, clear rig.settled when rig.dist crosses BOB_RANGE in rebuildNear, or never early-out before the first in-range bob.
verifyReason: Confirmed. spawn PivotTo's every kind to ground*(RideHeight+0.3) (623-624) and anchors Parked, Dealership and HotDrop at that height (675-676). EventService's HotDrop 'final' pose is that same pivot. In WheelAnimator, RANGE=250 but BOB_RANGE=140. A car first animated between 140 and 250 gets target 0, is marked settled (366), and the anchored early-out (307-312) never re-bobs it. rebuildNear never clears settled. Result: tyres float 0.3 studs off the road.
fix: In src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau spawn, compute `anchored` before the PivotTo and use `ride + (if anchored then 0 else 0.3)`. In src/client/Controllers/WheelAnimator.luau rebuildNear: record `local wasFar = rig.dist > BOB_RANGE` before updating rig.dist, and set rig.settled = false if wasFar and rig.dist <= BOB_RANGE.

summary: Nitro flame, drift smoke, tyre screech and the horn are client-only. Other players, including pursuers and spectators, never see or hear another player's nitro, drift or honk.
evidence: VehicleClient.luau:8-10 says 'Purely local; no remotes fired from here'. The FX are built in buildFx (VehicleClient.luau:568-663) and toggled in renderStep (VehicleClient.luau:889-923). honk() uses only a local Sound (VehicleClient.luau:1188-1214). The boosting and drifting state lives only in the client controller (VehicleController.luau:650-651, 720).
failureScenario: In a 5★ chase the fleeing player hits nitro and drifts round a corner. To the friend filming, the car just speeds up and slides silently. The 'moments worth clipping' pillar loses its most visible driving moments.
suggestedFix: Drift smoke can be derived from replicated velocity on observers (lateral slip from AssemblyLinearVelocity in WheelAnimator or EffectsController). For nitro and horn, add a rate-limited unreliable remote (VehicleFx: boosting on/off, honk) and have the server re-broadcast it with fireNear. Render it in EffectsController for other players' cars.
verifyReason: Confirmed. VehicleClient says it fires no remotes; nitro flame, drift smoke and screech are built and toggled locally; honk is a local Sound; boosting and drifting live only in the client controller. EffectsController and WheelAnimator have no FX for other cars. The integration doc lists 'Horn is local-only' as a known issue. The SPEC calls these 'local effects', so this is a polish gap rather than a bug.
fix: Derive drift smoke and screech for observers from replicated chassis velocity (lateral slip from AssemblyLinearVelocity) in src/client/Controllers/EffectsController.luau. The driver cannot set attributes on the server-owned model, so add a rate-limited unreliable remote 'VehicleFx' {boost:boolean, honk}. The server validates that the sender drives the car and re-broadcasts with fireNear; EffectsController renders it for other players' cars.

summary: Crash damage compares two velocity samples without using the real time between them. A server hitch or a burst of replication can turn hard braking or a nitro launch into false crash damage.
evidence: VehicleService.luau:1735-1738: the accumulator resets to 0 every ≥0.1 s regardless of the actual dt. damagePass (VehicleService.luau:1437-1458) uses raw Δv between samples, and _crashDamage (VehicleService.luau:409-415) uses a threshold of 55 studs/s. Brake plus handbrake is about 104 studs/s² (Config/Vehicle.luau:20 + VehicleController.luau:35).
failureScenario: A mobile client stalls for 0.6 s while braking from 120 studs/s. The server then sees a 62 studs/s drop in one sample and applies 4 damage with a health-bar pop, even though nothing was hit. It is rare, but it feels unfair when it happens repeatedly on bad connections.
suggestedFix: Track the time of the last sample and require Δv/Δt > ~550 studs/s² (an impact-level deceleration), or scale the threshold by max(1, Δt/0.1). Alternatively, confirm impacts with a server-side Touched or contact check on the chassis.
verifyReason: Confirmed. The damage accumulator resets to 0 on each ≥0.1 s tick (1735-1738). damagePass compares raw flat Δv between samples with no elapsed time, and the threshold is 55. Brake plus handbrake is about 104 studs/s², so a replication gap or server hitch of about 0.53 s or more during hard braking, or about 0.31 s during a hypercar nitro launch (accel 100×1.8), crosses 55 and applies phantom damage. Rare.
fix: In src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau, store st.lastVelAt and pass elapsed = now - st.lastVelAt into _crashDamage(prev, vel, elapsed?), defaulting to DAMAGE_TICK so the existing tests still pass. Use threshold = CRASH_DAMAGE_THRESHOLD * max(1, elapsed / DAMAGE_TICK).

summary: The suspension force is computed once per frame and held for the whole frame. Clamping dt only changes the maths, not how long the force acts. In simulation the spring diverges and launches the car at a sustained 8 FPS or lower.
evidence: VehicleController.luau:569 clamps dt to [1/240, MAX_DT], but the VectorForces set at VehicleController.luau:617 act for the real frame time (VehicleClient.luau:1089-1091 steps on PreSimulation). With SPRING_K=68 and SPRING_C=4.2 (Config/Vehicle.luau:14-15), my sampled-hold simulation settles at 60, 30, 20, 15 and 10 FPS and diverges at 8 FPS.
failureScenario: A low-end phone stuck at about 8 FPS (heavy streaming or a thermally throttled device) sees its car start bouncing and then launch into the air.
suggestedFix: When the real dt is greater than MAX_DT, scale the spring and damper terms by MAX_DT/dt, or switch to a critically damped target-height formulation. Alternatively, run the suspension on RunService.Stepped substeps.
verifyReason: The math and code path are confirmed. The suspension accel (K·comp + C·compVel) does not depend on dt, so clamping dt to MAX_DT has no effect on it. The forces are set once per PreSimulation (VehicleClient 1089) and held for the whole simulated frame. A zero-order-hold analysis with ω²=4K=272 and c=4C=16.8 gives a spectral radius of 0.90 at 9 FPS and 1.57 at 8 FPS, which matches the tracer. Whether it really diverges depends on how much simulated time Roblox advances per frame at about 8 FPS (the engine may throttle). The 0..4g force clamp also bounds it to a hop rather than a true launch. The tracer's 'Stepped substeps' alternative does not exist: Stepped is PreSimulation and fires once per frame.
fix: In src/shared/Vehicle/VehicleController.luau step(): when dtIn > Tuning.MAX_DT, let s = MAX_DT/dtIn and compute the suspension as staticSupport + K·(comp - staticComp)·s² + C·compVel·s, so the static load stays the same and the effective ωT matches 30 FPS. Add a settle-simulation case at 1/8 s in tests/spec/vehicle.spec.luau.

summary: As expected, the hero vehicle shells are loaded but nothing uses them. Each car ships one hero shell in ReplicatedStorage. Wiring them in needs several non-obvious steps, or every car breaks.
evidence: AssetLibrary.start loads every Assets.Hero entry (AssetLibrary.luau:236-266; Assets.luau:27-61, 33 keys that all match car ids including police_unit). No file reads AssetLibrary or Assets.Hero (grep finds only init.server ORDER), and CarBuilder.buildDef (CarBuilder.luau:1871-1911) has no hero hook, unlike what ART_PASS.md:22-27 describes. _normalize sets every part Anchored=true (AssetLibrary.luau:121) and adds a non-Massless, Anchored AssetRoot (AssetLibrary.luau:140-151). Shells are fitted to Assets.size (for example 12 for the rustbucket), not the car's Length attribute.
failureScenario: Today the art pass simply doesn't show, and replication carries 33 unused hero shells. If someone naively clones and welds the template, the anchored parts and AssetRoot anchor every car (it becomes undrivable) and add mass. Mutation colours wouldn't apply (no Paint attributes), sirens and headlights would be hidden, and baked mesh wheels wouldn't spin or steer.
suggestedFix: Wire it in CarBuilder.buildDef, or in VehicleService.spawn plus the display builders. Clone the template; destroy AssetRoot; set Anchored=false, Massless=true, CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch=false and CollisionFidelity=Box on every part; scale to the model's Length; align the bottom to pivot - RideHeight; weld to the Chassis with WeldConstraints; hide only the Paint=primary/accent/glass body parts while keeping the Chassis, seat, bump stops, Headlight/Taillight/Siren parts and the procedural wheels (or hide the mesh wheels); tag the shell Paint=primary and clear TextureID so applyMutation works; set HeroMesh=true. Hook AssetLibrary.Ready so cars and displays spawned before loading finishes are re-skinned. Check seat and head clearance inside each shell.
verifyReason: Confirmed but expected: the art pass (task #4) is pending, and vehicles-world.md 'Known issues' already says hero shells aren't applied. AssetLibrary.start loads all 33 Assets.Hero entries into ReplicatedStorage.AssetLibrary, so every client receives them, and nothing consumes them. CarBuilder.buildDef has no hero hook, unlike what ART_PASS.md:22-27 describes. Small correction: _normalize sets every part Massless=true (121); only AssetRoot is anchored and non-massless. The integration pitfalls the tracer lists (anchored parts and AssetRoot, Paint attributes, lights/sirens, wheels) are valid.
fix: For now: keep Hero templates out of replication until they are used (load Hero only after the CarBuilder hook exists, or publish them under ServerStorage) in src/server/Systems/AssetLibrary.luau. For the art pass: in src/shared/Vehicle/CarBuilder.luau buildDef (or VehicleService.spawn plus the display builders), clone the template and destroy AssetRoot. On every part set Anchored=false, Massless=true and CanCollide/CanQuery/CanTouch=false. Scale to the Length attribute, align the bottom to the ground plane, and WeldConstraint to Chassis. Hide only the Paint body parts and keep Chassis, seat, BumpStops, lights, sirens and the procedural wheels. Tag the shell Paint=primary and clear TextureID for mutations, set HeroMesh=true, and re-skin cars spawned before AssetLibrary.AllReady.

summary: On phones the SPIKES touch button (Scale-anchored at 36% height) slides down onto the EXIT button (offset-anchored 270 px from the bottom). DrivingUI draws above CombatHUD, so a tap meant for spikes ejects you from the car.
evidence:
CombatClient.luau:845-848: `sb.button.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0.5)`, `sb.button.Position = UDim2.new(1, -28, 0.36, 0)`, size 92. Its caption sits 2 px below the button (550-557).

Kit.luau:98-99 floors UIScale at 0.55, so the design canvas H on a phone is (viewport.Y minus insets)/0.55, about 565–645, not 720.

- H=565 (iPhone with home-indicator inset): the overlap is about 38 design px, and the 'SPIKES' caption lies entirely on EXIT.
DrivingUI uses DisplayOrder HUD+1 (VehicleClient.luau:273); CombatHUD uses HUD (CombatClient.luau:834). EXIT calls VehicleClient.exit(), which sets Jump=true (1178-1186). The integration note checked this layout only at 720.
failureScenario: A phone player who owns Spike Strips is in a 3★ getaway in a stolen car. They tap the lower half of SPIKES, the tap lands on EXIT, and they jump out. The theft goes to 'dropped' and the cops bust them on foot.
suggestedFix: Anchor SPIKES to the bottom like the rest of the driving cluster, e.g. UDim2.new(1,-156,1,-150) above DRIFT and left of NITRO. Better, move the button into DrivingUI's Touch frame so one module owns the cluster's layout. Add a layout test for canvas heights 560–650.
verifyReason: I confirmed the geometry. SpikeButton (CombatClient.luau:845-848) uses AnchorPoint (1,0.5) at (1,-28,0.36,0) with size 92, so it spans y 0.36H-46..0.36H+46 and x W-120..W-28. EXIT (VehicleClient.luau:465, AnchorPoint (1,1) from roundButton) spans H-354..H-270 at x W-124..W-40. They overlap whenever 0.36H+46 > H-354, which means a canvas height below 625; the SPIKES caption overlaps below about 659. Nothing repositions either button later (grep). gameplay-client.md:118 only checked this at 720.
fix: In CombatClient.start (src/client/Controllers/CombatClient.luau ~845-848), anchor SPIKES to the bottom-right cluster instead of 36% height: `sb.button.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 1)` and `sb.button.Position = UDim2.new(1, -144, 1, -170)`. That puts it left of HORN (W-124..W-40, H-254..H-170) and above DRIFT (top at H-128), with the caption clear of both, at any canvas height. Check that canvas heights 540-720 show no overlap with EXIT, HORN, NITRO or DRIFT.

summary: On PC the Roblox player list is open by default, because leaderstats exist. CoreGui draws it over the top-right corner, which is where the HUD puts the wanted stars, the 'GETTING BUSTED' bar and the whole toast stack.
evidence:

- HUDController.luau:806-814: bust bar at (1,-12,0,62).

summary: The driving speedometer is pinned 12 px above the screen bottom, directly under the CoreGui backpack hotbar, which stays visible and on top while seated. The nitro bar, health bar, rev bar and, on phones, the lower half of the MPH digits are covered.
failureScenario: On a phone (scale 0.55) the speedometer is about 86 px tall with its bottom about 7 px above the edge, and the 50–60 px hotbar slot covers the bars, the rev bar and the lower half of the digits. With bat, Zapper and Spikes the slots span almost the full speedometer width. Mid-chase the player can't see nitro charge or how close the car is to wrecking. On PC at 720p the bat slot covers the bar icons and the centre.

Or raise the speedometer by the same hotbar clearance HUDController computes, and shift THEFT_BOTTOM and CARD_BOTTOM up by the same amount.
verifyReason: The speedometer is anchored (0.5,1) at (0.5,0,1,-12), 340x156, so it spans H-168..H-12 (VehicleClient.luau:283-289). The bars sit at H-44..H-20 and the rev bar at H-70..H-50. summary: The DRIFT! banner sits in the same rectangle as the thief's 'DELIVER IT HOME!' countdown and draws on top of it. During the tutorial's first drive, the tutorial card covers the drift banner in turn.
evidence:

failureScenario: A player turns on STREAMER MODE to clip a 5★ chase or a Hot Drop. The clip still has toasts, feed lines naming other players, a 740-px 'HOT DROP' banner, 140-stud light pillars and edge arrows, so pillar 3 ('moments worth clipping') isn't served.

summary: On PC the default TextChatService window (top-left, open by default) sits over the HUD's CODES/SETTINGS row, the top of the menu column, the streamer-mode 👁️ button and the entire event feed.
evidence:

- TextChatService is in use (AdminService.luau:27, 617-635), and nothing sets ChatWindowConfiguration or disables chat.
failureScenario: On PC, chat messages overlay STORE, GEAR and INDEX. Feed lines like 'X stole Y's GOLD PHANTOM GT!' are unreadable under chat, and clicks on the covered buttons can land on chat. In streamer mode the only 'show HUD' button sits under the chat.
suggestedFix: Set TextChatService.ChatWindowConfiguration.VerticalAlignment = Bottom (or reposition it) from the client. Or start the HUD column and the feed below the chat window's height on desktop, e.g. move the feed to bottom-left above the hotbar.

On desktop the default chat window is open at the top-left under the top bar, and CoreGui draws above PlayerGui. The HUD puts the CODES/SETTINGS TopRow at (12,6) (HUDController.luau:857-864), the menu column from about y=72 at x=12, the streamer 👁️ toggle at (12,6) (921-933), and the event feed at (92,74), 400 wide and 160 tall (NotificationController.luau:51-53). In HUDController.layout (src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau ~962-993), start the TopRow and menu below the chat window: use TextChatService.ChatWindowConfiguration.AbsolutePosition/AbsoluteSize when ChatWindowConfiguration.Enabled, or a fixed desktop offset of about 260 design px with 2 columns via gridFit. summary: On phones the left menu column wraps into a 2–3 column grid of large buttons that reaches into the dynamic thumbstick's activation zone and stays visible while driving. The event feed, positioned for the 1-column desktop layout, draws over columns 2–3.
evidence:
- HUDController.luau:80: TOUCH_THUMB_REAL_PX = 120 assumes the thumbstick only uses the bottom 120 px.
- HUDController.luau:962-988 (layout) and gridFit (259-266) fill `canvasHeight - menuTop - reserve` and widen into more columns.
- Roblox's DynamicThumbstick frame covers roughly the left 40% from about a third of the screen height down. On an 844x390 phone the 3x3 grid of 76-design cells (x 12..252, y 82..322 design) lands at about x 7..139 and y 100..235 real px, overlapping a zone that starts near y 130.
- homeState (245-247) hides only HOME while driving; the menu stays.
- NotificationController.luau:51: FEED_ANCHOR x=92 at DisplayOrder 40 lands on columns 2–3 (x 94..252).
failureScenario: A phone player rests their thumb upper-left to start moving or to steer in a chase and opens GEAR or DAILY instead. The full-screen Menus backdrop (DisplayOrder 20, MenuController.luau:3111-3125) then covers the driving controls and thumbstick. Feed text also renders on top of the menu icons.
suggestedFix: On touch, lay the menu out as a horizontal strip under CODES/SETTINGS, or cap the column at y < H/3. Collapse it behind a single ☰ button while the Driving attribute is true. Position the feed from menu.AbsoluteSize, or move it right-centre on touch.
verifyReason: I confirmed this. layout() (HUDController.luau:962-993) uses menuTop=82, reserve=ceil(120/0.55)=219 and 76 px cells. At canvas H≈565-603, gridFit gives 3 rows × 3 columns, spanning x 12..252 and y 82..322 design, which is about x 7..139 and y 103..235 real px below the 58 px inset. The PlayerModule DynamicThumbstick frame covers the left 40% from 1/3 of the height down (y ≥ ~130 on a 390 px screen), and touches on GUI buttons are processed, so they don't start the stick. The bottom two rows of the grid sit inside that zone. TOUCH_THUMB_REAL_PX=120 wrongly assumes only the bottom 120 px matter. The menu is never hidden while driving: applyFocus only hides it in tutorial focus, and homeState hides only HOME. FEED_ANCHOR x=92 at DisplayOrder 40 draws dark feed rows over columns 2-3 (x 94..252, y 82..234).
fix: In HUDController (src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau): on touch, hide u.menu while the Driving attribute is true (keep the TopRow), and cap the grid so its bottom stays above canvasHeight/3 + inset. For example, compute `reserve` from 2/3 of the canvas instead of TOUCH_THUMB_REAL_PX, letting gridFit widen into more columns. In NotificationController (src/client/Controllers/NotificationController.luau), position the feed from the HUD menu's right edge, e.g. via an exported HUDController.getMenuRight(), or move it to the right-centre on touch.

- WaypointController.luau:916-921: insets are only 54 design px (116 on the left).

- VehicleClient.luau:283-289: the speedometer (DisplayOrder 11, opaque panel) covers bottom-centre 340x156 design.
- VehicleClient.luau:459-466: NITRO/DRIFT/HORN/EXIT cover the right edge from H-354 down.
failureScenario: Right after hotwiring a car that faces away from home, which is the normal case, the DROP OFF arrow should point the player around, but it is drawn under the speedometer. The tutorial's 'Follow the arrow into your garage' (TutorialController.luau:84) shows no arrow.
