summary: World BillboardGuis are sized in raw pixels and AlwaysOnTop, so on phones the waypoint marker covers about a third of the screen height and rarity tags and popups take about a third of the width. They ignore the 0.55 UI scale every ScreenGui uses.
evidence:
- WaypointController.luau:444-452: Marker `Size = UDim2.fromOffset(MARKER_WIDTH, 134)` (230x134), AlwaysOnTop, no MaxDistance.
- EffectsController.luau:1110-1119: RarityTag `UDim2.fromOffset(460, 66)`, AlwaysOnTop, with a 19-px auto-sized pill of about 290 px.
- NotificationController.luau:821-830: CashPopup 260x80, AlwaysOnTop.
- EffectsController.luau:631-642 and 729: comic bubbles 220x140, ×1.5 for BIG STEAL.
WaypointController already computes the UI scale (267-274) but applies it only to the edge arrows.
failureScenario: A phone player driving to the drop-off has a 134-px pin, label and distance block on top of the road and the garage door. In Rush Hour, several Rare+ tags in traffic cover the street, through buildings.
suggestedFix: Multiply billboard offset sizes by computeUiScale() (or use studs-based Size with a UISizeConstraint). Fade or shrink the marker within about 40 studs and give it a MaxDistance.
verifyReason: I confirmed the sizes. The waypoint Marker is UDim2.fromOffset(230,134), AlwaysOnTop, with no MaxDistance (WaypointController.luau:444-452). The RarityTag is 460x66 with a 19 px auto-sized pill, AlwaysOnTop, MaxDistance 165 (EffectsController.luau:1110-1119). CashPopup is 260x80. BillboardGui offsets are in GUI points, and none of these apply the 0.55 phone scale that ScreenGuis use. So on an 844x390 phone the marker is about 1/3 of the screen height and a tag pill about 1/3 of the width, drawn through buildings. computeUiScale already exists in WaypointController but only scales the arrows.
fix: In WaypointController (src/client/Controllers/WaypointController.luau), apply computeUiScale() to the Marker: set billboard.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(MARKER_WIDTH*s, 134*s) and add a UIScale (Scale=s) under a root frame holding pin, label and distance. Update both whenever uiScale changes in update(). Do the same for RarityTag in buildTag (src/client/Controllers/EffectsController.luau) and CashPopup (src/client/Controllers/NotificationController.luau). Optionally fade the marker within about 30 studs.

summary: Controllers that never added a touch multiplier render important text at about 6–11 real px on phones: toasts can shrink to 6 px, feed lines are about 9 px, event pills about 11 px, and the Hot Drop banner details about 9–10 px.
failureScenario: A phone player gets 'Garage full! Sell a car or chop it at the Chop Shop' as a roughly 7-px, three-line toast that disappears after 3.5s. They keep idling in the drop-off without knowing why nothing happens.
suggestedFix: Apply a touch DeviceScale of about 1.3–1.4 (the Tutorial pattern) to HC_Notifications, EventsHUD, DrivingUI labels and the HUD theft panel, or add a minEffectiveScale option to Kit.screen. Shorten toast copy and set MinTextSize so it is at least about 14 real px.
fix: Add an optional minimum effective scale to Kit.screen (src/client/UI/Kit.luau), e.g. Kit.screen(name, order, {touchMin = 0.72}), so touch devices use math.max(s, touchMin). Use it for HC_Notifications (src/client/Controllers/NotificationController.luau), EventsHUD (src/client/Controllers/EventsClient.luau) and DrivingUI (src/client/Controllers/VehicleClient.luau). Check that phone layouts still fit after this; the toast and feed widths may need to shrink. Alternatively, add a DeviceScale UIScale of about 1.3 to the toast stack, feed, pills and banner (the TutorialController pattern).

summary: The Rebirth menu's confirm fires a single Rebirth remote. Net's token bucket always drops the first call at 0.5/s, so the button shows 'REBIRTHING...' for 3s and reverts with no feedback (already noted as REBIRTH-RATE-LIMIT-DROPS-FIRST; the client gives no recovery hint).
evidence:
- RebirthService.luau:303-306 registers Net.on("Rebirth", ..., 0.5).
- Net.luau:100-107 creates the bucket with tokens = perSecond (0.5) and rejects when tokens < 1.
- MenuController.luau:2812-2827 fires once, on the second tap.
- MenuController.luau:2834-2840 silently re-enables the button after PENDING_SECONDS.
failureScenario: A player who has saved for a rebirth taps REBIRTH and then TAP AGAIN TO CONFIRM. Nothing happens and there's no toast. They must repeat both taps, which looks like a broken button.
suggestedFix: Initialise buckets with math.max(1, perSecond), or register Rebirth at 1/s. The client could also toast 'Try again' when the pending state times out without a Rebirths change.
verifyReason: This is a duplicate of REBIRTH-RATE-LIMIT-DROPS-FIRST (docs/integration/findings_contracts.json), which I re-verified. Net.allow creates the bucket with tokens=perSecond=0.5, refills it to min(1, 0.5+0)=0.5 on the first call and rejects when below 1. RebirthService registers at 0.5/s (303-305). MenuController fires Rebirth once on the confirm tap (2812-2817), and tick silently re-enables the button after PENDING_SECONDS (2834-2840). The first-ever rebirth per server session is dropped without feedback; a retry at least 1 s later works.
fix: In Net.allow (src/shared/Net.luau:100), initialise new buckets with `tokens = math.max(1, perSecond)`, which also protects any future sub-1 rates. Alternatively register Rebirth at 1/s in src/server/Systems/RebirthService.luau; RebirthService already has its own busy guard. Track this under the existing REBIRTH-RATE-LIMIT-DROPS-FIRST finding rather than as a new item.

summary: While your garage is locked and you're outside it, GarageHUD's lock pill (DisplayOrder 11) overlaps the HOME button (DisplayOrder 10) on phones and at 720p, and takes taps on HOME's lower half. Tapping the pill in the 'locked' or 'cooldown' state gives no feedback.
evidence:
- GarageClient.luau:649-655: LockButton AnchorPoint (0.5,1), Position (0.5,0,1,-112), 250x58, so H-170..H-112.
- GarageClient.luau:686: `btn.Visible = not driving and (inside or locked)`.
- GarageClient.luau:657-662: it only acts when lockState=='ready'.

suggestedFix: Show the lock pill only inside the garage and show the remaining lock time as a chip on HOME, or stack the two using HUDController.getBottomClearance(). Give non-ready taps a click sound and toast.
verifyReason: I confirmed this. LockButton (GarageClient.luau:649-655) uses AnchorPoint (0.5,1) at (0.5,0,1,-112), 250x58, so it spans H-170..H-112 at DisplayOrder 11. It is visible when `not driving and (inside or locked)` (686), so while the garage is locked and you're outside, it shows alongside HOME (homeState is 'ready' or 'wanted' outside the garage). HOME (AnchorPoint (0.5,1), bottom = ceil(74/s)+6) spans H-134..H-80 at s=1 (22 px overlap) and H-205..H-141 on touch at s=0.55 (29 px overlap). The pill is wider than HOME and on top of it. Taps in 'locked' or 'cooldown' state do nothing (657-662).

When locked and outside, either hide it or stack it above HOME using HUDController.getBottomClearance(), e.g. Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, -(clearance + 8)). summary: Menus close on Escape/ButtonB only through UserInputService.InputBegan. Roblox reserves Esc for its own system menu, and the Android back button opens the Roblox menu, but nothing hooks GuiService.MenuOpened.
evidence: MenuController.luau:3458-3466: InputBegan checks KeyCode.Escape or ButtonB and calls MenuController.close(). There is no GuiService.MenuOpened connection anywhere in src.
failureScenario: A PC player presses Esc to leave the Gear Shop. Roblox's in-game menu opens on top while the shop (and its backdrop) stays open underneath. Android back behaves the same way.
suggestedFix: Connect GuiService.MenuOpened to MenuController.close(), add a keyboard alternative such as Backspace or M, and keep ButtonB.
verifyReason: MenuController's only close-by-key path is UserInputService.InputBegan on Escape/ButtonB (3458-3466), and src has no GuiService.MenuOpened connection (grep). Roblox reserves Esc and the Android back button for its own system menu, so pressing Esc opens the Roblox menu whether or not InputBegan also fires. When the player returns, the shop and its backdrop are still open in most cases. This is minor: the X button and a backdrop tap still close menus, and gamepad B works.
fix: In MenuController.start (src/client/Controllers/MenuController.luau ~3458), add `GuiService.MenuOpened:Connect(function() if current then MenuController.close() end end)`. Optionally also accept KeyCode.Backspace as a keyboard close key.

summary: Announce banners (740x150 design, scale-pop and rotate) appear at 45% screen height and queue up to 6 at about 3s each. They cover the road mid-chase, worst on phones.
evidence: NotificationController.luau:56-57 (BANNER_POSITION = (0.5, 0.45)), 493-503 (banner build), 620-648 (about 2.25–3s hold each) and 676-678 (queue capped at 6).

BANNER_POSITION is (0.5,0.45); the banner is 740x150 design (about 407x82 real on an 844x390 phone, roughly half the width); it is held 1.1-2.25 s plus about 0.75 s of pop and fade (bannerHold, 129-136); the queue is capped at 6. Nothing changes this while Driving. This is a design trade-off for announcements rather than a defect, so I rate it low.

summary: Every Monetization id is 0, yet garage pads 11–12 permanently advertise '🅿️ +2 SLOTS PASS'. The pass can't be bought and no prompt appears, so it is a visible dead end (SPEC §9 hides id-0 items in the Store).
evidence:
- GarageClient.luau:401-402 sets the pass label whenever PassOnly is true.
- GarageClient.luau:457 only creates the purchase prompt when `Monetization.Passes.slots.id ~= 0`.
- Config/Monetization.luau sets every id to 0 (lines 13–89), and the Store shows 'coming soon'.

suggestedFix: When Passes.slots.id == 0, render those pads as '🔒 MAX' or hide them (PlotService/GarageService _padInfo could treat id 0 as not offered).
verifyReason: I confirmed this. renderPad labels every PassOnly pad '🅿️ +2 SLOTS PASS' (GarageClient.luau:401-402), but creates the prompt only when Monetization.Passes.slots.id ~= 0 (457). Every id in Config/Monetization.luau is 0, and the Store hides id-0 items per SPEC. The pads advertise something that can't be bought. summary: (Known, but it shows up in this client scenario.) StateController.sanitizeTheft strips dropped and droppedEndsAt. When the thief is knocked out of the car, the HUD keeps showing the long delivery countdown instead of a 'GET BACK IN! 0:12' state.
evidence: StateController.luau:86-96 returns only active, endsAt, carId and targetPlot. TheftService.luau:539-549 sends dropped and droppedEndsAt. HUDController.applyTheft and refreshTheft (1303-1342) can only show endsAt.

suggestedFix: Keep dropped and droppedEndsAt in sanitizeTheft. In HUDController, swap the title to 'GET BACK IN!' with a red countdown while dropped is true.
verifyReason: This is a duplicate of THEFTSTATE-DROPPED-STRIPPED, which I re-verified. TheftService.sendThiefState (534-549) sends dropped and droppedEndsAt, but StateController.sanitizeTheft (86-96) keeps only active, endsAt, carId and targetPlot. The HUD therefore can only show the long endsAt countdown. The one existing cue is the 'GET BACK IN!' waypoint label (TheftService ~551).

In src/client/Controllers/StateController.luau, keep `dropped = raw.dropped == true` and a finite numeric droppedEndsAt in sanitizeTheft and the TheftState type. In HUDController.applyTheft/refreshTheft (src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau ~1303-1342), while dropped, show 'GET BACK IN!' with a red countdown to droppedEndsAt.

summary: HUDController.gearAffordable ignores passes.taser, while the Gear Shop treats the Zapper as owned through the pass. Once pass ids are live, Zapper Pass owners get a permanent red '!' on GEAR for a tool they already own.
evidence:
- HUDController.luau:225-230 checks only `not tools[id] and cash >= def.price`.
- MenuController.luau:530 sets `owned = tools[id] == true or (id == "taser" and passes.taser == true)`.
failureScenario: A VIP who bought the Zapper Pass and has $15K sees the GEAR badge pulse and wiggle every 4s. Opening the menu shows ✅ OWNED, so the badge is noise.
suggestedFix: Reuse MenuController.toolRows' ownership rule in gearAffordable, or check snapshot.passes.taser for 'taser'.
verifyReason: I confirmed this. HUDController.gearAffordable (225-230) checks only `not tools[id]`. MenuController.toolRows (530) and ShopService (156) treat taser as owned when the Zapper Pass is held. CombatService.ownedTools grants it at runtime without writing data.tools.taser (711-713), so snapshot.tools.taser stays nil for pass holders. The bug is dormant while the pass id is 0.
fix: In HUDController.gearAffordable (src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau ~225), read `local passes = if typeof(snapshot.passes) == 'table' then snapshot.passes else {}` and skip a tool when `tools[id] or (id == 'taser' and passes.taser == true)`, matching MenuController.toolRows.

summary: (Extends known PERF-07.) WheelAnimator updates the 25 nearest cars every PreRender with no on-screen check: up to 4 bob raycasts within 140 studs and 4 Weld.C0 writes per car, including server-owned moving traffic and police assemblies. This is the largest steady per-frame client cost on low-end phones.
evidence:
- WheelAnimator.luau:26-28: HOT_COUNT=25, COLD_PER_FRAME=6.
- 425-441: the hot list updates every frame.
- 339-355: raycast per wheel while dist ≤ BOB_RANGE.
- 364: `w.weld.C0 = ...` per wheel per frame.
- 254-277: rebuildNear selects by distance only, with no frustum test.
Other loops (Sound scan at 4 Hz, Effects tags at 4 Hz, Dealership's 8 CFrame writes, Waypoints) are bounded. I found no leaks.
failureScenario: In Rush Hour (36 traffic cars) plus a 4★ chase with police, a low-end Android phone does about 100 raycasts and 100 joint writes per frame on top of the local VehicleController. This causes frame drops right when driving needs to feel best (pillar 2).
suggestedFix: Skip cars whose chassis is off-screen (WorldToViewportPoint), use HOT_COUNT of about 8 on touch, bob-raycast every second or third frame, and prefer Motor6D.Transform over Weld.C0 for per-frame wheel poses.
verifyReason: This duplicates the known PERF-07 (findings_security_perf.json). I re-verified the constants: HOT_COUNT 25, COLD_PER_FRAME 6, BOB_RANGE 140. The hot list is updated every PreRender (425-441) with a per-wheel raycast within BOB_RANGE (339-355) and a weld.C0 write per wheel (364). rebuildNear selects by distance only, with no frustum or device-tier check (254-277). The only new detail is that police assemblies are included, which the existing finding already implies.
